title.zh: 卷四百七十六 列傳第二百三十五 叛臣中 李全上
title.en: Volume 476 Biographies 235: Rebellious Officials 2 - Li Quan 1
title.raw: 卷四百七十六 列傳第二百三十五 叛臣中 李全上 Volume 476 Biographies 235: Rebellious Officials 2 - Li Quan 1

sentences.zh: 叛臣中○李全上

translations.literal: Rebellious Officials (continued) ○ Li Quan, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious Officials (continued): Li Quan, Part One

sentences.zh: 李全者，濰州北海農家子，同產兄弟三人。

translations.literal: Li Quan was a farmer's son from Beihai in Weizhou, with three brothers from the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan was a peasant's son from Beihai in Weizhou; he had three full brothers.

sentences.zh: 全銳頭蜂目，權譎善下人，以弓馬趫捷，能運鐵槍，時號“李鐵槍”。

translations.literal: Quan had a sharp head and bee-like eyes, was crafty and good at winning people over, was swift with bow and horse, could wield an iron spear, and was called at the time "Li the Iron Spear."
translations.idiomatic: He had a narrow, pointed head and prominent eyes, was shrewd and skilled at winning followers, excelled at archery and horsemanship, and could wield a heavy iron spear; people called him "Li the Iron Spear."

sentences.zh: 初，大元兵破中都，金主竄汴，賦斂益橫，遺民保岩阻思亂。

translations.literal: At first, when the Great Yuan army captured Zhongdu, the Jin ruler fled to Bian, levies grew ever more oppressive, and survivors who held mountain strongholds thought of revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Mongol armies took Zhongdu, the Jin emperor fled to Kaifeng, taxes and exactions grew ever harsher, and displaced people sheltering in mountain fastnesses began to turn against the regime.

sentences.zh: 於是劉二祖起泰安，掠淄、沂。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Erzu rose at Tai'an and raided Zi and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Erzu rose in Tai'an and raided Zibo and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 二祖死，霍儀繼之。

translations.literal: When Erzu died, Huo Yi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzu died, Huo Yi took his place.

sentences.zh: 彭義斌、石珪、夏全、時青、裴淵、葛平、楊德廣、王顯忠等附之。

translations.literal: Peng Yibin, Shi Gui, Xia Quan, Shi Qing, Pei Yuan, Ge Ping, Yang Deguang, Wang Xianzhong, and others joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yibin, Shi Gui, Xia Quan, Shi Qing, Pei Yuan, Ge Ping, Yang Deguang, Wang Xianzhong, and others rallied to his banner.

sentences.zh: 楊安兒起，掠莒、密，展徽、王敏為謀主，母舅劉全為帥，汲君立、王琳、閻通、董友、張正忠、孫武正等附之，餘寇蜂起。

translations.literal: Yang An'er rose, raided Ju and Mi, with Zhan Hui and Wang Min as strategists, his maternal uncle Liu Quan as commander, and Ji Junli, Wang Lin, Yan Tong, Dong You, Zhang Zhengzhong, Sun Wuzheng, and others joining him; other bandits swarmed forth everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yang An'er also rose, raiding Ju and Mi; Zhan Hui and Wang Min served as his strategists, his maternal uncle Liu Quan as commander, and Ji Junli, Wang Lin, Yan Tong, Dong You, Zhang Zhengzhong, Sun Wuzheng, and others attached themselves to him, while bandits erupted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 大元兵至山東，全母及其兄死焉。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army reached Shandong, Quan's mother and his elder brother died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Mongol forces reached Shandong, Quan's mother and his elder brother were killed.

sentences.zh: 全與仲兄福聚眾數千，劉慶福、國安用、鄭衍德、田四、于洋、洋弟潭等咸附之。

translations.literal: Quan and his second elder brother Fu gathered several thousand men; Liu Qingfu, Guo Anyong, Zheng Yande, Tian Si, Yu Yang, Yang's younger brother Tan, and others all joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and his second brother Fu mustered several thousand followers; Liu Qingfu, Guo Anyong, Zheng Yande, Tian Si, Yu Yang, Yu Yang's younger brother Tan, and others all rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 大元兵退，金乃遣完顏霆為山東行省，黃摑為經曆官，將花帽軍三千討之，敗安兒於闌頭滴水，斷其南路。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army withdrew, Jin sent Wanyan Ting as Shandong Branch Secretariat, Huang Gui as administrative officer, and led three thousand Flower-Cap troops to suppress them; they defeated An'er at Lantou Dishui and cut off his southern route.
translations.idiomatic: After the Mongols withdrew, the Jin court sent Wanyan Ting as Shandong commissioner and Huang Gui as his administrative officer with three thousand Flower-Cap troops to suppress the rebels; they defeated An'er at Lantou Dishui and severed his southern line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 安兒輕舸走即墨，金人募其頭千金，舟人斬以獻。

translations.literal: An'er fled in a light boat to Jimo; the Jin offered a thousand gold for his head, and a boatman beheaded him and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: An'er fled in a light boat toward Jimo; the Jin posted a thousand-piece reward for his head, and a boatman killed him and turned it in.

sentences.zh: 安兒無子，從子友偽稱“九大王”，不閑軍務。

translations.literal: An'er had no son; his nephew You falsely styled himself "Ninth Great King" and did not attend to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An'er had no son; his nephew You falsely styled himself the Ninth Great King and left military affairs unattended.

sentences.zh: 安兒妹四娘子狡悍善騎射，劉全收潰卒奉而統之，稱曰“姑姑”，眾尚萬餘，掠食至磨旗山，全以其眾附，楊氏通焉，遂嫁之。

translations.literal: An'er's younger sister, the Fourth Lady, was cunning and fierce and skilled at riding and shooting; Liu Quan gathered scattered troops and installed her as leader, calling her "Auntie"; her force still numbered more than ten thousand; they foraged as far as Mojishan; Quan attached his troops to her, became intimate with Lady Yang, and then married her.
translations.idiomatic: An'er's younger sister, known as the Fourth Lady, was fierce and skilled with bow and horse; Liu Quan rallied scattered troops around her and had them call her "Auntie." Her force still numbered more than ten thousand, and they foraged as far as Mojishan. Quan brought his men under her banner, grew close to Lady Yang, and eventually married her.

sentences.zh: 全合軍與霆戰，又敗。

translations.literal: Quan combined his army and fought Ting again, and was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Quan united his forces and fought Ting again, only to be defeated once more.

sentences.zh: 霆驍將張惠望見全，躍馬赴之，槍及全，若有縶其馬足而止者。

translations.literal: Ting's fierce general Zhang Hui saw Quan, leaped his horse toward him, and his spear reached Quan, yet it was as if something held his horse's feet and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's fierce general Zhang Hui spotted Quan, spurred his horse toward him, and drove his spear at him; yet it was as though something had seized the horse's legs and held him back.

sentences.zh: 全得收餘眾保東海，劉全分軍駐固上。

translations.literal: Quan was able to gather the remnant troops and hold Donghai; Liu Quan divided his army and encamped at Gushang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan rallied his survivors and held Donghai, while Liu Quan detached a force and encamped at Gushang.

sentences.zh: 霍儀攻沂州不下，霆自清河出徐州，斬儀，潰其眾。

translations.literal: Huo Yi attacked Yizhou but could not take it; Ting advanced from Qinghe toward Xuzhou, beheaded Yi, and routed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yi besieged Yizhou without success; Ting marched from Qinghe toward Xuzhou, executed Yi, and scattered his army.

sentences.zh: 彭義斌歸李全。

translations.literal: Peng Yibin submitted to Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yibin then submitted to Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 黃摑者，即阿魯達。

translations.literal: Huang Gui was Aruda.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gui was in fact Aruda.

sentences.zh: 霆即李二措，賜姓完顏。

translations.literal: Ting was Li Ercuo, granted the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was Li Ercuo, to whom the Jin had granted the surname Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 惠號“賽張飛”，燕俠士也。

translations.literal: Hui was styled "Rival to Zhang Fei" and was a Yan warrior.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was nicknamed "Rival to Zhang Fei" and was a warrior from Yan.

sentences.zh: 此數人者，出沒島固，寶貨山委而不得食，相率食人。

translations.literal: These several men lurked on the islands and in the marshes; treasure piled up like mountains yet they could not eat, and they led one another to eat human flesh.
translations.idiomatic: These men lurked among the coastal islands and marshes; though treasure lay heaped like hills, they had nothing to eat and turned to cannibalism together.

sentences.zh: 有沈鐸者，鎮江武鋒卒也，亡命盜販山陽，誘致米商，斗米輒售數十倍，知楚州應純之償以玉貨，北人至者輒舍之。

translations.literal: There was one Shen Duo, a soldier of the Wufeng Army in Zhenjiang, who fled as an outlaw and smuggled at Shanyang, luring in rice merchants and selling a dou of rice for several tens of times the price; knowing that Ying Chunzhi of Chuzhou paid in jade goods, he would lodge any northerner who came.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Shen Duo, a soldier of Zhenjiang's Wufeng Army, who fled into outlawry and smuggled at Shanyang. He lured rice merchants in and sold a dou of rice for many times the usual price. Learning that Ying Chunzhi of Chuzhou paid in jade goods, he gave shelter to any northerner who arrived.

sentences.zh: 又說純之以歸銅錢為名，弛度淮之禁，來者莫可遏。

translations.literal: He also urged Chunzhi, under the pretext of repatriating copper cash, to relax the prohibition on crossing the Huai, so that arrivals could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded Chunzhi, on the pretext of recovering copper cash, to relax restrictions on crossing the Huai, so that arrivals could no longer be checked.

sentences.zh: 安兒之未敗也，有意歸宋，招禮宋人。

translations.literal: Before An'er's defeat, he had intended to submit to Song and treated Song men with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Before his defeat, An'er had intended to submit to the Song and treated Song subjects with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 定遠民季先者，嘗為大俠劉佑家廝養，隨佑部綱客山陽，安兒見而說之，處以軍職。

translations.literal: Ji Xian of Dingyuan had once been a household servant of the great knight Liu You; he followed You's transport escort to Shanyang; An'er saw him and was pleased with him, and gave him a military post.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xian of Dingyuan had once served as a household retainer to the great knight Liu You and accompanied You's transport escort to Shanyang. An'er took a liking to him and gave him a military post.

sentences.zh: 安兒死，先至山陽，寅緣鐸得見純之，道豪傑願附之意。

translations.literal: When An'er died, Xian went to Shanyang and, through Duo's connections, obtained an audience with Chunzhi and conveyed the wish of the heroes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After An'er died, Xian went to Shanyang and, through Duo's connections, gained an audience with Chunzhi to convey the northern heroes' wish to submit.

sentences.zh: 時江、淮制置李玨、淮東安撫崔與之皆令純之沿江增戍，恐不能禦，乃命先為機察，諭意群豪；

translations.literal: At the time the Jiang-Huai commissioner Li Jue and the Huaidong pacification commissioner Cui Yuzhi both ordered Chunzhi to increase garrisons along the river, fearing they could not hold the line; they therefore appointed Xian as intelligence officer to convey their intent to the various heroes;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jiang-Huai commissioner Li Jue and the Huaidong pacification commissioner Cui Yuzhi both ordered Chunzhi to strengthen riverine defenses, fearing they could not hold the line. They therefore appointed Xian as intelligence officer to convey their intent to the various heroes;

sentences.zh: 敘復鐸為武鋒軍副將，辟楚州都監，與高忠皎各集忠義民兵，分二道攻金。

translations.literal: they restored Duo to deputy commander of the Wufeng Army, appointed him Chuzhou garrison commander, and had him and Gao Zhongjiao each gather loyalist militia and attack Jin by two routes.
translations.idiomatic: restored Duo to deputy commander of the Wufeng Army, appointed him Chuzhou garrison commander, and had him and Gao Zhongjiao each raise loyalist militia to attack Jin along two routes.

sentences.zh: 先遂以李全五千人附忠皎，合兵攻克海州，糧援不繼，退屯東海。

translations.literal: Xian then attached Li Quan's five thousand men to Zhongjiao; their combined forces captured Haizhou, but grain supplies did not follow, and they withdrew to encamp at Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then attached Li Quan's five thousand men to Zhongjiao; together they took Haizhou, but supplies failed to follow and they withdrew to Donghai.

sentences.zh: 全分兵襲破莒州，禽金守蒲察李家，別將于洋克密州，兄福克青州，始授全武翼大夫、京東副總管。

translations.literal: Quan divided his troops and stormed Juzhou, capturing the Jin defender Pucha Li Jia; his subordinate Yu Yang took Mizhou, and his elder brother Fu took Qingzhou; Quan was first appointed Grand Master for Exalted Martial Affairs and deputy overall commander of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Quan detached troops and stormed Juzhou, capturing the Jin defender Pucha Li Jia; his lieutenant Yu Yang took Mizhou and his elder brother Fu took Qingzhou. Quan was then appointed Grand Master for Exalted Martial Affairs and deputy overall commander of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 純之見北軍屢捷，密聞於朝，謂中原可復。

translations.literal: Chunzhi, seeing the northern armies win repeatedly, secretly reported to court that the Central Plains could be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the northern armies win repeatedly, Chunzhi secretly reported to court that the Central Plains could be recovered.

sentences.zh: 時頻歲小稔，朝野無事，丞相史彌遠鑒開禧之事，不明招納，密敕玨及純之慰接之，號“忠義軍”，就聽節制。

translations.literal: At the time there had been several years of modest harvests and court and countryside were untroubled; Chancellor Shi Miyuan, taking warning from the Kaixi affair, did not openly recruit them, but secretly ordered Jue and Chunzhi to comfort and receive them; they were styled the "Loyalist Army" and were placed under local command.
translations.idiomatic: Several years of modest harvests had left court and countryside at ease. Chancellor Shi Miyuan, mindful of the Kaixi debacle, did not openly recruit them but secretly ordered Jue and Chunzhi to receive and reassure them. They were styled the Loyalist Army and placed under local command.

sentences.zh: 於是有旨依武定軍生券例，放錢糧萬五千人，名“忠義糧”。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict followed the precedent of the Wuding Army ration certificates and issued money and grain for fifteen thousand men, called "Loyalist rations."
translations.idiomatic: An edict then followed the Wuding Army ration-certificate precedent and issued money and grain for fifteen thousand men under the name "Loyalist rations."

sentences.zh: 於是東海馬良、高林、宋德珍等萬人輻湊漣水，鐸納之，全與劉全俱起羨心焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ma Liang, Gao Lin, Song Dezhen, and others from Donghai, ten thousand men, converged on Lianshui; Duo received them, and both Quan and Liu Quan grew envious.
translations.idiomatic: Then Ma Liang, Gao Lin, Song Dezhen, and others from Donghai—ten thousand men in all—converged on Lianshui, and Duo took them in, stirring envy in both Quan and Liu Quan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十一年五月己丑，全軍至漣水，邀先白事楚城，取器甲金穀，議再攻海州，純之厚勞全金玉器用及其下有差。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiading, fifth month, day jichou, Quan's army reached Lianshui; he invited Xian to report at Chucheng, took weapons, armor, gold, and grain, and discussed attacking Haizhou again; Chunzhi richly rewarded Quan with gold, jade, utensils, and graded gifts for his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the fifth month in the eleventh year of Jiading, Quan's army reached Lianshui. He invited Xian to report at Chucheng, took weapons, armor, gold, and grain, and discussed another assault on Haizhou. Chunzhi richly rewarded Quan with gold, jade, and utensils and gave graded gifts to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 六月，全圍海城，金經略阿不罕、納不刺等固守不下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Quan besieged Haicheng; the Jin commissioners Abuhan, Nabuci, and others held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Quan besieged Haicheng, but the Jin commissioners Abuhan, Nabuci, and others held firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 七月，合鄆、單、邳、徐兵來援，全與戰於高橋，不勝，退守石秋，分兵襲密州，禽黃摑，械至楚城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month combined troops from Yan, Shan, Pi, and Xu came to relieve the city; Quan fought them at Gaoqiao, was defeated, withdrew to hold Shiqiu, divided troops to raid Mizhou, captured Huang Gui, and sent him in fetters to Chucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month relief forces from Yan, Shan, Pi, and Xu arrived; Quan fought them at Gaoqiao, was beaten, withdrew to Shiqiu, detached troops to raid Mizhou, captured Huang Gui, and sent him in chains to Chucheng.

sentences.zh: 是冬，徙屯淮陰之龜山。

translations.literal: That winter he moved his camp to Guishan in Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he shifted his camp to Guishan in Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 十二年，山東來歸者不止，權楚州梁丙無以贍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, submitters from Shandong kept arriving without cease, and Acting Chuzhou prefect Liang Bing had no means to support them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year submitters from Shandong kept arriving, and Acting Chuzhou prefect Liang Bing could not feed them all.

sentences.zh: 先懇丙請預借兩月，然後帥所部五千並良等萬人往密州就食，不許；

translations.literal: Xian earnestly asked Bing to advance two months' rations, then lead his five thousand men together with Liang's ten thousand to Mizhou for provisions; this was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Xian pleaded with Bing to advance two months' rations so he could lead his five thousand men, together with Liang's ten thousand, to Mizhou for provisions; Bing refused;

sentences.zh: 請速遣全代領其眾，又不許。

translations.literal: he asked that Quan be sent quickly to take command of his force, and this too was refused.
translations.idiomatic: he then asked that Quan be sent at once to take command of his force, and that too was refused.

sentences.zh: 丙以石珪權軍務，珪乃奪運糧之舟，二月庚辰，率軍二萬度淮大掠。

translations.literal: Bing put Shi Gui in charge of military affairs; Gui then seized grain-transport boats, and on day gengchen of the second month led twenty thousand troops across the Huai on a great raid.
translations.idiomatic: Bing placed Shi Gui in charge of military affairs. Gui seized grain-transport boats and, on the gengchen day of the second month, led twenty thousand troops across the Huai on a great raid.

sentences.zh: 丙調王顯臣、高友、趙邦永以兵逆之，至南度門，顯臣敗，友、邦永遇珪，下馬與作山東語，皆不復戰。

translations.literal: Bing mobilized Wang Xianchen, Gao You, and Zhao Bangyong with troops to oppose him; at Nandu Gate Xianchen was defeated; You and Bangyong met Gui, dismounted, and spoke with him in Shandong dialect, and none fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Bing sent Wang Xianchen, Gao You, and Zhao Bangyong to oppose him. At Nandu Gate Xianchen was defeated; You and Bangyong met Gui, dismounted, and spoke with him in Shandong dialect, and none of them fought again.

sentences.zh: 丙窘，乃遣全出諭之。

translations.literal: Bing, in distress, then sent Quan out to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Bing, hard pressed, sent Quan out to reason with him.

sentences.zh: 時金人圍淮西急，馬司都統李慶宗戍濠，出戰，喪騎三千，珪及張春皆有亡失。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin were pressing the siege of western Huai; the Horse Bureau commander-in-chief Li Qingzong garrisoned Hao, went out to fight, and lost three thousand horsemen; both Gui and Zhang Chun also suffered losses.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were then pressing hard on western Huai. Horse Bureau commander Li Qingzong, garrisoning Hao, went out to fight and lost three thousand horsemen; Gui and Zhang Chun also suffered losses.

sentences.zh: 帥司調全與先、珪軍援盱眙。

translations.literal: The commandery staff ordered Quan, together with the armies of Xian and Gui, to relieve Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery staff ordered Quan, together with the armies of Xian and Gui, to relieve Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 全亦欲自試，親往東海點軍赴之。

translations.literal: Quan also wished to test himself and went in person to Donghai to muster troops and hurry to the front.
translations.idiomatic: Quan also wished to prove himself and went in person to Donghai to muster troops for the relief.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，遇金人於嘉山，戰小捷。

translations.literal: On day guihai he met Jin troops at Jiashan and won a small victory.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day he met Jin troops at Jiashan and won a minor victory.

sentences.zh: 三月，先軍進駐天長，全進駐盱眙，鼎立以待金人。

translations.literal: In the third month Xian's army advanced and encamped at Tianchang, Quan's at Xuyi, standing like a tripod to await the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xian advanced to Tianchang and Quan to Xuyi, forming a tripod of positions to await the Jin.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，全至渦口，值金將乞石烈牙吾答名“盧鼓槌”者將濟，全與其將鹿仙掩之，金兵溺淮者數千，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: On day yiyou Quan reached Wokou and encountered the Jin general Qishilie Yayuda, styled "Lu the Drum-Mallet," about to cross; Quan and his general Lu Xian ambushed him; several thousand Jin soldiers drowned in the Huai, and captives were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Quan reached Wokou and found the Jin general Qishilie Yayuda, nicknamed "Lu the Drum-Mallet," about to cross the river. Quan and his general Lu Xian ambushed him; several thousand Jin soldiers drowned in the Huai, and the captives were many.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，與阿海戰於化陂湖，大捷，殺金數將，得其金牌，追至曹家莊而還。

translations.literal: On day renchen he fought Ahai at Huabihu in a great victory, killed several Jin generals, obtained his gold plaque, and pursued as far as Caojiazhuang before returning.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day he fought Ahai at Huabihu in a great victory, killed several Jin generals, seized his gold plaque, and pursued as far as Caojiazhuang before returning.

sentences.zh: 三圍俱解，全喪失亦眾。

translations.literal: All three sieges were lifted, but Quan's losses were also heavy.
translations.idiomatic: All three sieges were lifted, though Quan's own losses were heavy as well.

sentences.zh: 阿海者，金所謂四駙馬也。

translations.literal: Ahai was what the Jin called one of the Four Imperial Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Ahai was one of the Jin's Four Imperial Sons-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 全進達州刺史，妻楊氏封令人。

translations.literal: Quan was promoted to prefect of Dazhou, and his wife Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady Lingren.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was promoted to prefect of Dazhou, and his wife Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady Lingren.

sentences.zh: 六月，金元帥張林以青、莒、密、登、萊、濰、淄、濱、棣、寧海、濟南十二州來歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Jin commander Zhang Lin submitted with the twelve prefectures of Qing, Ju, Mi, Deng, Lai, Wei, Zi, Bin, Di, Ninghai, and Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Jin commander Zhang Lin submitted twelve prefectures—Qing, Ju, Mi, Deng, Lai, Wei, Zi, Bin, Di, Ninghai, and Jinan.

sentences.zh: 始，林心存宋，及摑敗，意決而未能達。

translations.literal: At first Lin kept Song in his heart; when Gui was defeated his resolve was settled but he could not yet carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had long favored returning to the Song; when Gui was captured his resolve hardened, but he could not yet act on it.

sentences.zh: 會全還濰州上塚，揣知林意，乃薄兵青州城下，陳說國家威德，勸林早附。

translations.literal: When Quan returned to Weizhou to tend his family's graves, he divined Lin's intent, drew his troops up under the walls of Qingzhou, set forth the state's majesty and virtue, and urged Lin to submit early.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan returned to Weizhou to tend his family's graves, he sensed Lin's intent, drew up his troops beneath Qingzhou's walls, expounded the Song's majesty and virtue, and urged Lin to submit at once.

sentences.zh: 林恐全誘己，猶豫未納。

translations.literal: Lin feared Quan was luring him and hesitated, not yet admitting him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin feared Quan was trying to trap him and hesitated to admit him.

sentences.zh: 全約挺身入城，惟數人從，林乃開門納之，相見甚歡，謂得所托，置酒結為兄弟。

translations.literal: Quan offered to enter the city alone with only a few followers; Lin then opened the gates and received him; they met very gladly; Lin said he had found one to rely on; they set out wine and became sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Quan offered to enter the city alone with only a few followers. Lin opened the gates and received him; they met with great warmth, Lin saying he had found someone to rely on, and they shared wine and became sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 全既得林要領，附表奉十二州版籍以歸。

translations.literal: Once Quan had grasped Lin's vital point, he attached a memorial presenting the registers of the twelve prefectures in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Once Quan had won Lin over completely, he submitted a memorial with the registers of the twelve prefectures.

sentences.zh: 表辭有云：“舉諸七十城之全齊，歸我三百年之舊主。

translations.literal: The memorial's wording said: "Raising all seventy cities of complete Qi, we return to our lord of three hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial declared: "Raising all seventy cities of complete Qi, we return to our lord of three hundred years."

sentences.zh: ”表，馮垍所作也。

translations.literal: " The memorial was composed by Feng Yong.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was composed by Feng Yong.

sentences.zh: 秋，授林武翼大夫、京東安撫兼總管，其餘授官有差。

translations.literal: In autumn Lin was appointed Grand Master for Exalted Martial Affairs, Jingdong pacification commissioner and overall commander; the rest received offices in graded fashion.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Lin was appointed Grand Master for Exalted Martial Affairs and Jingdong pacification commissioner and overall commander; the others received offices according to rank.

sentences.zh: 進全廣州觀察使、京東總管，劉慶福、彭義斌皆為統制，增放二萬人錢糧，徙屯楚州。

translations.literal: Quan was advanced to surveillance commissioner of Guangzhou and overall commander of Jingdong; Liu Qingfu and Peng Yibin were both made controllers; rations were increased for twenty thousand more men; and the army was moved to encamp at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guangzhou and overall commander of Jingdong; Liu Qingfu and Peng Yibin were made controllers; rations were increased for twenty thousand more men; and the army was shifted to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，制置使賈涉以朝命督戰，許殺金太子者，賞節度使；

translations.literal: Earlier, the commissioner Jia She, by court order supervising battle, had promised that whoever killed a Jin crown prince would be rewarded with the rank of military governor;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, commissioner Jia She, by court order supervising the campaign, had promised that whoever killed a Jin crown prince would receive the rank of military governor;

sentences.zh: 殺親王，承宣使；

translations.literal: whoever killed a prince of the blood, the rank of palace commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: whoever killed a prince of the blood, the rank of palace commissioner;

sentences.zh: 殺駙馬，觀察使。

translations.literal: whoever killed an imperial son-in-law, the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: and whoever killed an imperial son-in-law, the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 全致所得金牌於涉，云殺四駙馬所獲者。

translations.literal: Quan presented the gold plaque he had obtained to She, saying it was taken from killing one of the Four Imperial Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Quan presented the gold plaque he had taken to She, claiming he had killed one of the Four Imperial Sons-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 涉上於朝，乞如約賞之，故全有是受，而四駙馬實不死也。

translations.literal: She memorialized court and asked that the reward be given as promised; therefore Quan received the appointment, yet the Four Imperial Sons-in-Law had in fact not died.
translations.idiomatic: She memorialized court to grant the promised reward, and Quan received the appointment—yet the Four Imperial Sons-in-Law were in fact still alive.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大雨雪，淮冰合。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month there was heavy rain and snow, and the Huai froze solid.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month heavy rain and snow fell, and the Huai froze solid.

sentences.zh: 全請於制府曰：“每恨泗州阻水，今如平地矣，請取東西城自效。

translations.literal: Quan requested of the commandery staff: "I have always resented that Sizhou was blocked by water; now it is like level ground; I ask to take the eastern and western cities to prove my merit."
translations.idiomatic: Quan asked the commandery staff: "I have always resented that Sizhou was cut off by water; now it is like open ground. Let me take its eastern and western cities to prove my worth."

sentences.zh: ”制府遣就盱眙劉卓議，卓集諸將燕全，時青、夏全咸願以長槍三千人從。

translations.literal: " The commandery staff sent him to consult Liu Zhuo at Xuyi; Zhuo gathered the generals to feast Quan; Shi Qing and Xia Quan both wished to follow with three thousand long-spear troops.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery staff sent him to consult Liu Zhuo at Xuyi. Zhuo gathered the generals to feast Quan; Shi Qing and Xia Quan both offered three thousand long-spear troops to follow.

sentences.zh: 夜半度淮，潛向泗之東城，將踏濠冰傅城下，掩金人不備。

translations.literal: At midnight they crossed the Huai, stole toward the eastern city of Si, intended to tread the moat ice and reach the foot of the wall, and surprise the Jin unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they crossed the Huai and stole toward Si's eastern city, intending to cross the frozen moat to the wall and catch the Jin unprepared.

sentences.zh: 俄城上荻炬數百齊舉，遙謂曰：“賊李三！

translations.literal: Soon several hundred reed torches on the wall were raised together, and from afar they called: "Bandit Li the Third!
translations.idiomatic: Soon hundreds of reed torches blazed along the wall, and voices called from afar: "Bandit Li the Third!

sentences.zh: 汝欲偷城耶？

translations.literal: Do you mean to steal the city?
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to steal the city?

sentences.zh: ”天黑，故以火燭之。

translations.literal: " It was dark, so they used fire to illuminate him.
translations.idiomatic: " It was dark, so they lit torches to show him.

sentences.zh: 全知有備，引去。

translations.literal: Quan knew they were prepared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Quan saw they were ready and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十三年，趙拱以朝命諭京東，過青厓固，嚴實求內附。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhao Gong, by court order, went to instruct Jingdong; passing Qingyagu, Yan Shi sought to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhao Gong went to Jingdong on court orders; passing Qingyagu, Yan Shi sought to submit to the Song.

sentences.zh: 拱與定約，奉實款至山陽，舉魏、博、恩、德、懷、衛、開、相九州來歸。

translations.literal: Gong made a pact with him, escorted Shi's submission to Shanyang, and presented the nine prefectures of Wei, Bo, En, De, Huai, Wei, Kai, and Xiang in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Gong made a pact with him, escorted Shi's submission to Shanyang, and presented nine prefectures—Wei, Bo, En, De, Huai, Wei, Kai, and Xiang—in submission.

sentences.zh: 涉再遣拱往諭，配兵二千，全亦請往，涉不能止，乃帥楚州及盱眙忠義萬餘人以行。

translations.literal: She again sent Gong to instruct them, assigning two thousand troops; Quan also asked to go; She could not stop him and therefore led more than ten thousand loyalist troops from Chuzhou and Xuyi on the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: She sent Gong again with two thousand troops. Quan also asked to go, and She could not refuse; he led more than ten thousand loyalist troops from Chuzhou and Xuyi on the expedition.

sentences.zh: 拱說全曰：“將軍提兵度河，不用而歸，非示武也，今乘勢取東平，可乎？

translations.literal: Gong urged Quan: "General, you led troops across the river and returned without being used—this does not display martial prowess; now, riding the momentum to take Dongping—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: Gong urged Quan: "General, you led troops across the river and came back unused—that hardly shows your prowess. Why not seize Dongping while the moment is ripe?"

sentences.zh: ”於是全合林軍得數萬，襲東平之城南。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Quan combined with Lin's army to muster several tens of thousands and struck the southern wall of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then combined with Lin's army to muster tens of thousands and struck the southern wall of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 金參政蒙古剛帥眾守東平，全以三千人金銀甲、赤幟，繞濠躍馬索戰。

translations.literal: The Jin Grand Councilor Menggu Gang commanded the defense of Dongping; Quan with three thousand men in gold and silver armor and red banners circled the moat, leaped his horse, and challenged battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Grand Councilor Menggu Gang held Dongping. Quan led three thousand men in gilded armor with red banners, circled the moat on horseback, and challenged battle.

sentences.zh: 時大暑，全見城阻水，矢石不能及，乃與林夾汶水而砦，中通浮梁來往。

translations.literal: It was the height of summer; Quan saw the city blocked by water so arrows and stones could not reach, and therefore he and Lin encamped on either side of the Wen River, linked by a floating bridge for passage back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer Quan saw the city protected by water so that arrows and stones could not reach it. He and Lin encamped on either side of the Wen River, linked by a floating bridge.

sentences.zh: 一夕，汶水溢，漂大木，斷浮梁，全首尾幾絕，蓋金人堰汶水而決之也。

translations.literal: One night the Wen overflowed, carrying off great timbers and breaking the floating bridge; Quan was nearly cut off at both ends—for the Jin had dammed the Wen and breached it.
translations.idiomatic: One night the Wen overflowed, carrying off great timbers and breaking the bridge; Quan was nearly cut off at both ends—the Jin had dammed the Wen and breached it.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，金騎兵三百奄至，全欣然上馬，帥帳前所有騎赴之，殺數人，奪其馬，逐北抵山谷。

translations.literal: At dawn three hundred Jin horsemen suddenly arrived; Quan gladly mounted, led all the cavalry before his tent against them, killed several men, seized their horses, and pursued north to the mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn three hundred Jin horsemen suddenly appeared. Quan mounted gladly, led every horseman before his tent against them, killed several, seized their mounts, and pursued north into the hills.

sentences.zh: 上有龍虎上將軍者，貫銀甲，揮長槊，盛兵以出，旁有繡旗女將馳槍突鬥。

translations.literal: Above was the Dragon-Tiger General in silver armor, wielding a long spear, leading a great force out; beside him a female general with embroidered banners charged with spear in fierce combat.
translations.idiomatic: Above stood the Dragon-Tiger General in silver armor, wielding a long spear, leading a great force out; beside him a female general with embroidered banners charged with spear in fierce combat.

sentences.zh: 會諸將至，拔全以出，乃退保長清縣，精銳喪失太半，統制陳孝忠死焉。

translations.literal: When the other generals arrived they pulled Quan out; then they withdrew to hold Changqing County; elite troops were lost by more than half; the controller Chen Xiaozhong died there.
translations.idiomatic: When the other generals arrived they pulled Quan free and withdrew to Changqing County. More than half his elite troops were lost, and the controller Chen Xiaozhong was killed.

sentences.zh: 林兵還青州。

translations.literal: Lin's troops returned to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's troops returned to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 全所攜鎮江軍五百人多怨憤，全乃分隸拱，使先歸，而以餘眾道滄州，假鹽利以慰贍之。

translations.literal: Of the five hundred Zhenjiang troops Quan had brought, many were resentful; Quan therefore assigned them to Gong's command, had Xian return first, and led the rest by way of Cangzhou, borrowing salt profits to comfort and support them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the five hundred Zhenjiang troops Quan had brought were resentful. He assigned them to Gong, sent Xian back first, and led the rest by way of Cangzhou, using salt profits to support them.

sentences.zh: 龍虎上將軍者，東平副帥幹不搭；

translations.literal: The Dragon-Tiger General was Ganbuda, deputy commander of Dongping;
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon-Tiger General was Ganbuda, deputy commander of Dongping;

sentences.zh: 女將者，劉節使女也。

translations.literal: the female general was the daughter of Commissioner Liu.
translations.idiomatic: the female general was Commissioner Liu's daughter.

sentences.zh: 全至楚州，屬召先赴行在。

translations.literal: When Quan reached Chuzhou, orders arrived summoning Xian to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan reached Chuzhou, orders arrived summoning Xian to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 全自渦口之捷，有輕諸將心，獨先嘗策戰勳，威望不下己，患之。

translations.literal: Since his victory at Wokou Quan had looked down on the other generals; only Xian had once planned campaigns and won merit, and his prestige was not below Quan's—Quan resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Since his victory at Wokou Quan had grown contemptuous of the other generals. Only Xian had planned campaigns and won merit, and his prestige rivaled Quan's—Quan resented him.

sentences.zh: 乃陰結制帥所任吏莫凱，使譖先，先卒，全喜而心益貳。

translations.literal: He therefore secretly joined with Mo Kai, an official appointed by the commissioner, and had him slander Xian; Xian died; Quan rejoiced and his heart grew ever more disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly enlisted Mo Kai, an official appointed by the commissioner, to slander Xian. When Xian died, Quan rejoiced and his loyalty grew ever more doubtful.

sentences.zh: 涉乘先死，欲收其軍，輟統制陳選往漣水以總之。

translations.literal: She, taking advantage of Xian's death, wished to take over his army and detached the controller Chen Xuan to go to Lianshui to command it overall.
translations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of Xian's death, She sought to take over his army and sent the controller Chen Xuan to Lianshui to assume overall command.

sentences.zh: 先黨裴淵、宋德珍、孫武正及王義深、張山、張友拒而不受，潛迎石珪於盱眙，奉為統帥。

translations.literal: Xian's partisans Pei Yuan, Song Dezhen, Sun Wuzheng, Wang Yishen, Zhang Shan, and Zhang You refused and would not accept this; they secretly welcomed Shi Gui at Xuyi and installed him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's partisans Pei Yuan, Song Dezhen, Sun Wuzheng, Wang Yishen, Zhang Shan, and Zhang You refused to accept Chen and secretly welcomed Shi Gui at Xuyi as their commander.

sentences.zh: 珪道楚城，涉不知覺，及選還，涉恥之，乃謀分珪軍為六，請於朝，出修武、京東路鈐轄印告各六授淵等，使之分統，謂可散其縱。

translations.literal: Gui passed through Chucheng without She's knowledge; when Xuan returned, She was shamed by this and therefore plotted to divide Gui's army into six, requested court approval, issued six seals of the Xiuzhou and Jingdong circuit military commissioner and distributed them to Yuan and the others, making them divide command, thinking this could scatter their license.
translations.idiomatic: Gui passed through Chucheng without She's knowledge. When Xuan returned, She was shamed and plotted to divide Gui's army into six parts, petitioning court for six seals of the Xiuzhou and Jingdong circuit military commissioner to give Yuan and the others separate commands, hoping thus to break their power.

sentences.zh: 淵等陽受命，涉即聞於朝，謂六人已順從，珪無能為矣。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others outwardly accepted the orders; She immediately reported to court that the six men had submitted and Gui could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and the others outwardly accepted the orders. She immediately reported to court that the six had submitted and Gui was finished.

sentences.zh: 其後有教令皆不納，然後知淵等猶主珪，涉恐甚。

translations.literal: Afterward they would not accept any instructional orders; only then did She know Yuan and the others still upheld Gui, and She was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they refused every order from headquarters, and only then did She realize Yuan and the others still followed Gui. She was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 全結府吏伺知之，乃見涉，請討珪，涉未有處。

translations.literal: Quan had won over a staff official to spy on this; he then saw She and asked to campaign against Gui; She had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had enlisted a staff official to spy on the situation, then came to She and asked to campaign against Gui. She had no answer.

sentences.zh: 議者請以全軍布南度門，移淮陰戰艦陳於淮岸，以示珪有備，然後命一將招珪軍，來者增錢糧，不至罷支，眾心一散，珪黨自離。

translations.literal: Advisers asked that Quan's army be posted at Nandu Gate, that Huaiyin warships be moved and arrayed on the Huai bank to show Gui there was preparation, then that a general be ordered to recruit Gui's troops—increase pay and grain for those who came, cut off support for those who did not—so hearts would scatter at once and Gui's party would break apart of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers proposed posting Quan's army at Nandu Gate and lining Huaiyin warships along the Huai to show Gui they were ready, then sending a general to recruit his troops—more pay for those who came, none for those who did not—so morale would collapse and Gui's followers would drift away.

sentences.zh: 涉用其策，珪技果窮。

translations.literal: She adopted this plan, and Gui's stratagems were indeed exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: She adopted the plan, and Gui's options ran out.

sentences.zh: 珪素通好於大元，至是殺淵而挾武正、德珍與其謀主孟導歸大元。

translations.literal: Gui had long been on good terms with the Great Yuan; at this point he killed Yuan and took Wuzheng, Dezhen, and his strategist Meng Dao with him to submit to the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long been friendly with the Mongols. Now he killed Yuan and took Wuzheng, Dezhen, and his strategist Meng Dao with him to submit to them.

sentences.zh: 漣水軍未有所屬，全求並將之。

translations.literal: The Lianshui army had no commander; Quan asked to take it over as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Lianshui army lacked a commander, and Quan asked to take it over as well.

sentences.zh: 客有請以附淮將者，曰：“使南將主北軍，則淮、楚為一。

translations.literal: A guest suggested attaching it to a Huai general, saying: "If a southern general commands the northern army, then Huai and Chu become one."
translations.idiomatic: A guest suggested placing it under a Huai general, saying: "If a southern officer commands the northern troops, Huai and Chu become one."

sentences.zh: ”涉然之，且曰：“先在時有三千虛籍，今當遣明亮核實，因可省費。

translations.literal: " She agreed and also said: "When Xian was alive there were three thousand phantom rolls; now we should send Ming Liang to verify and thus save expense."
translations.idiomatic: She agreed and added: "When Xian was alive there were three thousand phantom rolls on the books. Send Ming Liang to verify them and we can save money."

sentences.zh: ”全聞之即獻計曰：“全若朝將此軍，夕與核除虛籍。

translations.literal: " When Quan heard this he immediately offered a plan: "If Quan takes this army in the morning, by evening he will verify and eliminate the phantom rolls."
translations.idiomatic: When Quan heard this he immediately offered: "If I take command in the morning, I will purge the phantom rolls by evening."

sentences.zh: ”因卑辭獻珍具以自結，涉不能卻，遂以付全。

translations.literal: " He therefore with humble words presented rare goods to win her over; She could not refuse and therefore handed the army over to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent rare gifts with humble words to win her over. She could not refuse and handed the army to Quan.

sentences.zh: 翼日，復命曰：“初謂有虛額，昨夕細點，萬五千人之外尚溢十數名。

translations.literal: The next day he reported back: "At first it was said there were phantom quotas; last night on careful count, beyond the fifteen thousand there were still more than ten extra names."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reported: "We expected phantom quotas, but last night's count found more than ten men beyond the fifteen thousand already on the rolls."

sentences.zh: ”涉始悟全見紿，他日議更遣幕屬點之。

translations.literal: " She then realized Quan had deceived her and another day discussed sending a staff member to count again.
translations.idiomatic: She then realized Quan had deceived her and planned to send a staff officer to recount the rolls.

sentences.zh: 吏亟報全，全忽狀白涉：“昨夕三鼓，漣水告警，云金人萬餘在邳州。

translations.literal: The official quickly reported to Quan; Quan suddenly memorialized She: "Last night at the third watch Lianshui raised the alarm, saying more than ten thousand Jin were at Pizhou."
translations.idiomatic: The official quickly warned Quan, who suddenly memorialized She: "Last night at the third watch Lianshui reported more than ten thousand Jin at Pizhou."

sentences.zh: 全思漣水去邳咫尺，既無險阻，城壁復弊，一被攻劫，則直臨淮面，罪在全矣。

translations.literal: Quan reflected that Lianshui was only a short distance from Pi, had no natural barriers, and its walls were again dilapidated; if it were attacked and overrun, the enemy would come straight to the Huai face-to-face—the blame would fall on Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Lianshui lies only a short march from Pi, with no natural defenses and crumbling walls. If it falls, the enemy will be on the Huai at once—and the blame will be mine.

sentences.zh: 深夜不敢驚制使，已調七千人迎敵矣。

translations.literal: In the deep night he dared not disturb the commissioner and had already mobilized seven thousand men to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I dared not wake the commissioner at this hour and have already mobilized seven thousand men to meet them.

sentences.zh: ”涉知全詐，因寢點軍之議。

translations.literal: " She knew Quan was deceiving her and therefore dropped the plan to count the troops.
translations.idiomatic: She saw through the ruse and dropped the plan to recount the troops.

sentences.zh: 全又白制府請於朝，以劉全為總管駐揚州，分數千兵從之，而將其眾。

translations.literal: Quan again reported to the commandery staff and requested of court that Liu Quan be made overall commander stationed at Yangzhou, with several thousand troops detached to follow him, while Quan himself would command the main body.
translations.idiomatic: Quan also petitioned court through the commandery to make Liu Quan overall commander at Yangzhou with several thousand detached troops, while he retained command of the main force.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁未，全遊金山，作佛事，以薦國殤。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day dingwei, Quan toured Jinshan and performed Buddhist rites to commend the nation's war dead.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the eleventh month Quan visited Jinshan and held Buddhist rites for the nation's war dead.

sentences.zh: 知鎮江府喬行簡方舟逆之，大合樂以饗之。

translations.literal: The Zhenjiang prefect Qiao Xingjian met him in a linked fleet of boats and assembled great music to feast him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang prefect Qiao Xingjian met him in a fleet of boats and staged a lavish musical feast.

sentences.zh: 總領程覃迭為主禮，務訁誇北人以繁盛。

translations.literal: The fiscal intendant Cheng Tan took turns as chief host, striving to boast to the northerners of southern prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal intendant Cheng Tan took turns as host, straining to impress the northerners with southern prosperity.

sentences.zh: 全請所狎娼，覃不與，全歸，語其徒曰：“江南佳麗無比，須與若等一到。

translations.literal: Quan asked for a courtesan he favored; Tan would not give her; Quan returned and told his followers: "The beauties of Jiangnan are beyond compare; you must come with me there once."
translations.idiomatic: Quan asked for a courtesan he favored; Tan refused. On returning, Quan told his men: "Jiangnan's beauties are beyond compare—you must come with me there."

sentences.zh: ”始造舭達舟，謀爭舟楫之利焉。

translations.literal: " He then began building boda boats, plotting to compete for mastery of shipping profits.
translations.idiomatic: He then began building boda boats, plotting to seize control of river shipping profits.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，金人將南來，全請於涉，欲與劉卓共圖泗州，以伐其謀，涉許之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year the Jin were about to march south; Quan asked She that he and Liu Zhuo jointly take Sizhou to thwart their plan; She agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, as the Jin prepared to march south, Quan asked She to let him and Liu Zhuo take Sizhou and thwart their plan. She agreed.

sentences.zh: 全兵至盱眙度淮，攻克泗州之西城，入城布守。

translations.literal: Quan's troops reached Xuyi, crossed the Huai, captured the western city of Sizhou, entered the city, and deployed garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's troops reached Xuyi, crossed the Huai, took Sizhou's western city, and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 卓徙盱眙芻粟以實之，防城之具俱撤以往，為必守之計。

translations.literal: Zhuo moved Xuyi's fodder and grain to fill it, and all defensive equipment was withdrawn and sent there, as a plan to hold it at all costs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo stripped Xuyi of fodder and grain to stock the city and sent all defensive equipment there, planning to hold it at all costs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，盧鼓槌來取西城，全盛兵出戰，大敗，統制賴興死，全閉城自守。

translations.literal: Before long Lu the Drum-Mallet came to retake the western city; Quan led his full force out to fight, was greatly defeated, the controller Lai Xing died, and Quan shut the gates to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lu the Drum-Mallet came to retake the western city. Quan led his full force out, was routed, and the controller Lai Xing was killed. Quan shut the gates and held on.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，不勝，全遁歸，資糧器械悉以委敵。

translations.literal: The next day he fought again, was not victorious, Quan fled back, and supplies, grain, and weapons were all abandoned to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fought again and lost. Quan fled, abandoning all supplies, grain, and weapons to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 金人既陷蘄州，扈再興、趙範及其弟葵邀擊於天長。

translations.literal: After the Jin had taken Qizhou, Hu Zaiying, Zhao Fan, and his younger brother Kui intercepted them at Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin took Qizhou, Hu Zaiying, Zhao Fan, and Fan's younger brother Kui intercepted them at Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 全隨行襲金人後，謁而賀曰：“二監軍已立大功，乞以餘寇付全追之。

translations.literal: Quan followed along and struck the Jin rear; he called on them and congratulated them, saying: "The two supervisory generals have already won great merit; I beg that the remnant bandits be given to Quan to pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Quan followed and struck the Jin rear, then called on them and said: "You two have already won great merit. Give me the remnant enemy to pursue."

sentences.zh: ”然全追之不甚力，亦以是進承宣使。

translations.literal: " Yet Quan did not pursue very hard and was nevertheless promoted to palace commissioner on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he pursued halfheartedly and was nevertheless promoted to palace commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，卓再取西城，盧鼓槌背城力戰，戒惠必獲全，不獲則斬。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Zhuo again took the western city; Lu the Drum-Mallet fought with his back to the wall and warned Hui that he must capture Quan or be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year Zhuo retook the western city. Lu the Drum-Mallet fought with his back to the wall and warned Hui that he must capture Quan or be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 惠數嘗敗全於山東，而不能獲，每歎曰：“天假此賊，事未可量。

translations.literal: Hui had several times defeated Quan in Shandong but could not capture him, and would sigh each time: "Heaven lends this bandit life; the outcome cannot yet be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Hui had defeated Quan several times in Shandong but never captured him, and would sigh: "Heaven lends this bandit life—the outcome is still uncertain."

sentences.zh: ”及聞盧鼓槌言，自度進未必獲，退復受戮，即陳躍馬奔全壁，棄所執兵請降。

translations.literal: " When he heard Lu the Drum-Mallet's words, he judged that advancing might not secure a capture and retreating would again bring execution; he therefore declared himself, leaped his horse toward Quan's camp, cast aside his weapons, and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Lu's warning, he judged that advancing might not bring a capture and retreat would mean death. He spurred his horse to Quan's camp, cast aside his weapons, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 全掖而起之，相與歡甚。

translations.literal: Quan raised him up by the arm and they rejoiced together greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Quan raised him by the arm and they rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 不數日，惠戲下數千人皆潛至，全與惠歸，請於制置司官之，令自總一軍。

translations.literal: Within a few days several thousand of Hui's followers all arrived in secret; Quan returned with Hui, asked the commissionerate to grant him office, and had him command an army of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Within days several thousand of Hui's followers slipped in. Quan returned with Hui, had him commissioned, and gave him command of his own army.

sentences.zh: 膠西當登、寧海之衝，百貨輻湊，全使其兄福守之，為窟宅計。

translations.literal: Jiaoxi lay on the route between Deng and Ninghai; goods of every kind converged there; Quan had his elder brother Fu hold it as a plan for a lair and home base.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxi lay on the route between Deng and Ninghai, where goods of every kind converged. Quan stationed his elder brother Fu there as his base of operations.

sentences.zh: 時互市始通，北人尤重南貨，價增十倍。

translations.literal: At the time border trade had just opened; northerners especially valued southern goods, whose prices rose tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Border trade had just opened, and northerners prized southern goods so highly that prices rose tenfold.

sentences.zh: 全誘商人至山陽，以舟浮其貨而中分之，自淮轉海，達於膠西。

translations.literal: Quan lured merchants to Shanyang, floated their goods by boat and split them in half, and from the Huai turned to the sea to reach Jiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan lured merchants to Shanyang, shipped their goods by boat and took half, then sent them from the Huai by sea to Jiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 福又具車輦之，而稅其半，然後從聽往諸郡貿易，車、夫皆督辦於林，林不能堪。

translations.literal: Fu again provided carts and carriages and taxed half, then allowed them to trade in the various prefectures; carts and drivers were all requisitioned from Lin, and Lin could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu provided carts and taxed half again before allowing trade in the prefectures. Carts and drivers were all requisitioned from Lin, who could not endure the burden.

sentences.zh: 林財計仰六鹽場，福恃其弟有大造於林，又欲分其半，林許福恣取鹽，而不分場。

translations.literal: Lin's finances depended on six salt yards; Fu relied on his younger brother's great service to Lin and also wished to take half; Lin allowed Fu to take salt freely but would not share the yards.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's finances depended on six salt yards. Fu, relying on his brother's great service to Lin, also demanded half. Lin let Fu take salt freely but would not share the yards themselves.

sentences.zh: 福怒曰：“若背恩耶？

translations.literal: Fu angrily said: "Do you betray our kindness?
translations.idiomatic: Fu raged: "Do you betray our kindness?

sentences.zh: 待與都統提兵取若頭爾！

translations.literal: Wait until I bring troops with the overall commander to take your head!"
translations.idiomatic: Wait until I bring the overall commander's troops to take your head!"

sentences.zh: ”林懼，訴於制置司。

translations.literal: " Lin was afraid and appealed to the commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was terrified and appealed to the commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 涉密召林戲下問之，福伏兵於途以伺，林覺不追。

translations.literal: She secretly summoned Lin's followers to question them; Fu set an ambush on the road to watch for him; Lin sensed this and did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: She secretly summoned Lin's followers for questioning. Fu set an ambush on the road; Lin sensed the trap and did not go.

sentences.zh: 於是李馬兒說林歸大元，福狼狽走楚州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Ma'er persuaded Lin to submit to the Great Yuan; Fu fled in disarray to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Ma'er persuaded Lin to submit to the Mongols, and Fu fled in disarray to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，加全招信軍節度。

translations.literal: In winter Quan was further made military governor of the Zhaoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Quan was made military governor of the Zhaoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 林猶遺涉書詆全，明己非叛。

translations.literal: Lin still sent She a letter denouncing Quan and making clear he was not a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Lin still sent She a letter denouncing Quan and insisting he was no rebel.

sentences.zh: 涉以咎全，全請為朝廷取之，乃提師駐海州以迫林。

translations.literal: She blamed Quan for this; Quan asked to take it for the court on his own and therefore led his army to encamp at Haizhou to press Lin.
translations.idiomatic: She blamed Quan, who offered to recover the territory for the court and marched to Haizhou to pressure Lin.

sentences.zh: 涉間道遣黥胥王翊、閻瓊勞林，林泣涕道其故。

translations.literal: She sent by a secret route the tattooed clerk Wang Yi and Yan Qiong to comfort Lin; Lin wept and explained the cause.
translations.idiomatic: She sent the tattooed clerk Wang Yi and Yan Qiong by a secret route to comfort Lin, who wept as he explained what had happened.

sentences.zh: 翊歸，全使人殺諸塗。

translations.literal: When Yi returned, Quan had men kill them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, Quan had them killed on the road.

sentences.zh: 全攻林急，林走，全遂入青州。

translations.literal: Quan pressed the attack on Lin hard; Lin fled, and Quan then entered Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan pressed the attack; Lin fled, and Quan entered Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，涉勸農出郊，暮歸入門，忠義軍遮道，涉使人語楊氏，楊氏馳出門，佯怒忠義而揮之，道開，涉乃入城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year She went out to the suburbs to encourage agriculture; at dusk on her return at the gate the Loyalist Army blocked the road; She sent someone to speak to Lady Yang; Lady Yang rushed out the gate, feigned anger at the loyalists and waved them away, the road opened, and She then entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year She went out to encourage farming. At dusk on her return the Loyalist Army blocked the road. She sent word to Lady Yang, who rushed out, feigned anger at the loyalists and waved them aside, clearing the way for She to enter.

sentences.zh: 自是以疾求去甚力。

translations.literal: From this time she urgently sought leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she urgently sought leave on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 五月被召。

translations.literal: In the fifth month she was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month she was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 秋，全新置忠義軍籍。

translations.literal: In autumn Quan newly established Loyalist Army rolls.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Quan established new Loyalist Army rolls.

sentences.zh: 初，涉屯鎮江副司八千人於城中，翟朝宗統之；

translations.literal: At first She had stationed eight thousand men of the Zhenjiang deputy office in the city under Zhai Chaozong;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier She had stationed eight thousand men of the Zhenjiang deputy office in the city under Zhai Chaozong;

sentences.zh: 分帳前忠義萬人，屯五千城西，趙邦永、高友統之；

translations.literal: she divided ten thousand loyalists from her personal guard, stationed five thousand west of the city under Zhao Bangyong and Gao You;
translations.idiomatic: she split ten thousand loyalists from her personal guard, posting five thousand west of the city under Zhao Bangyong and Gao You;

sentences.zh: 屯五千淮陰，王暉及於潭統之，所以制北軍也。

translations.literal: and stationed five thousand at Huaiyin under Wang Hui and Yu Tan—all to control the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: and five thousand at Huaiyin under Wang Hui and Yu Tan—all to keep the northern army in check.

sentences.zh: 全輕鎮江兵，且以利啖其統制陳選及趙興，使不為己患；

translations.literal: Quan looked down on the Zhenjiang troops and also used profit to win over their controllers Chen Xuan and Zhao Xing so they would not become a threat to him;
translations.idiomatic: Quan despised the Zhenjiang troops and bribed their controllers Chen Xuan and Zhao Xing so they would not trouble him;

sentences.zh: 唯忌帳前忠義，乃數稱高友等勇，遇出軍必請以自隨，涉不許。

translations.literal: he only feared the loyalists of her personal guard; he repeatedly praised the bravery of Gao You and others, and whenever troops went out he always asked to take them along—She did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: but he feared She's personal loyalists. He repeatedly praised Gao You and others and always asked to take them on campaign—She refused.

sentences.zh: 全每燕戲下，並召涉帳前將校，帳前亦願隸焉，然未能合也。

translations.literal: Whenever Quan feasted his followers he also invited She's personal guard officers; the guard also wished to attach to him, yet they could not yet be united.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Quan feasted his followers he also invited She's guard officers, who wished to join him, but the merger had not yet happened.

sentences.zh: 及丘壽邁攝帥事，全忽請曰：“忠義烏合，尺籍鹵莽。

translations.literal: When Qiu Shoumai took charge of command affairs, Quan suddenly requested: "The loyalists are a mob; the rolls are careless and crude."
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Shoumai took interim command, Quan suddenly proposed: "The loyalists are a mob and the rolls are a mess."

sentences.zh: 莫若別置新籍，一納諸朝，一申制閫，一留全所，庶功過有考，請給無弊。

translations.literal: It would be better to set up separate new rolls—one copy to the court, one to the commandery staff, one kept at Quan's headquarters—so merit and fault can be examined and pay and grain issued without abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Better to create new rolls—one for court, one for headquarters, one for my command—so merit and fault can be tracked and pay issued without fraud."

sentences.zh: ”壽邁善而諾之。

translations.literal: " Shoumai approved and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shoumai approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 全乃合帳前忠義悉籍之，盡統其軍，時人莫悟。

translations.literal: Quan then enrolled all of She's personal loyalists in the rolls and took full command of their army; people at the time did not perceive his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then enrolled all of She's personal loyalists and took command of their entire force. No one yet saw what he was doing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，許國自武階換朝議大夫、淮東安撫制置使，命下，聞者驚異。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xu Guo was transferred from Wujie to Court Gentleman for Discussion and Huaidong pacification commissioner; when the order was issued, those who heard were startled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xu Guo was transferred from Wujie to Court Gentleman for Discussion and Huaidong pacification commissioner—an appointment that startled everyone who heard it.

sentences.zh: 先是，國奉祠家食，數言全必反，欲傾涉而代之。

translations.literal: Earlier Guo had lived at home on temple stipend and repeatedly said Quan would surely rebel, wishing to topple She and replace her.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo had lived at home on temple stipend and repeatedly warned that Quan would rebel, hoping to replace She.

sentences.zh: 會召國奏事，國疏全奸謀甚深，反狀已著，非有豪傑不能消弭，蓋自鬻也。

translations.literal: When he was summoned to report at court, Guo memorialized that Quan's treacherous schemes were very deep, signs of rebellion already clear, and only a hero could quell them—he was in effect selling himself.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to court he memorialized that Quan's treachery ran deep, rebellion was already evident, and only a hero could stop him—effectively selling himself for the post.

sentences.zh: 至是，喬行簡為吏部侍郎，上疏論國望輕，不宜帥淮，不報。

translations.literal: At this time Qiao Xingjian was vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and memorialized that Guo's standing was slight and he was unfit to command Huai—no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xingjian, now vice minister of Personnel, memorialized that Guo's standing was too slight to command Huai, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 山陽參幕徐晞稷雅意開閫，及聞國用，晞稷闕望，乃譽國奏注釋以寄全，全得報，不樂。

translations.literal: Xu Xiji, a staff officer at Shanyang, had long wished to open a command post; when he heard Guo was appointed, Xiji was disappointed in his hopes and therefore praised Guo in a memorial with annotations and sent it to Quan; when Quan received the report he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiji, a staff officer at Shanyang, had long hoped for a command post himself. When Guo was appointed, Xiji sent Quan a memorial praising Guo with annotations. Quan was not pleased.

sentences.zh: 是冬，金將李二措及邳州守致書海州，欲附宋，全戲下周岊得之，即以報全。

translations.literal: That winter the Jin general Li Ercuo and the defender of Pizhou sent a letter to Haizhou wishing to submit to Song; Quan's follower Zhou Yi obtained it and immediately reported to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jin general Li Ercuo and the Pizhou defender wrote to Haizhou offering to submit to the Song. Quan's follower Zhou Yi obtained the letter and reported at once.

sentences.zh: 全喜，遣王喜兒以兵二千應接，而己繼之。

translations.literal: Quan rejoiced and sent Wang Xi'er with two thousand troops to meet them, while he himself followed after.
translations.idiomatic: Quan rejoiced and sent Wang Xi'er with two thousand men to meet them, following with the main force.

sentences.zh: 二措納喜兒而囚之。

translations.literal: Ercuo received Xi'er and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ercuo received Xi'er and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 全兵欲攻邳，四面阻水，二措積勁弩備之，全不得進，合兵索戰。

translations.literal: Quan's troops wished to attack Pi but were blocked by water on all sides; Ercuo piled up powerful crossbows in defense; Quan could not advance and combined his forces to challenge battle.
translations.idiomatic: Quan tried to attack Pi but found it surrounded by water on all sides. Ercuo had massed powerful crossbows; Quan could not advance and challenged battle with his full force.

sentences.zh: 全敗，欲還楚州，會濱、棣有亂，乃引兵趨山東。

translations.literal: Quan was defeated, wished to return to Chuzhou, but as Bin and Di were in turmoil he therefore led his troops toward Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was defeated and meant to return to Chuzhou, but unrest in Bin and Di drew him instead toward Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，國之鎮，楊氏郊迓，國辭不見，楊氏慚以歸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year Guo took up his post; Lady Yang went out to the suburbs to welcome him; Guo declined and would not see her; Lady Yang returned in shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year Guo took up his post. Lady Yang went out to welcome him; Guo refused to see her, and she returned in shame.

sentences.zh: 國既視事，痛抑北軍，有與南軍競者，無曲直偏坐之，犒賚十裁七八。

translations.literal: Once Guo had assumed duties he harshly suppressed the northern army; when they competed with the southern army, regardless of right or wrong he always punished the northerners, and rewards were only seven or eight tenths of what was due.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office Guo harshly suppressed the northern army. In any dispute with southern troops he punished the northerners regardless of fault, and paid them only seven or eight tenths of their due rewards.

sentences.zh: 全自山東致書於國，國誇於眾曰：“全仰我養育，我略示威，即奔走不暇矣。

translations.literal: Quan from Shandong sent a letter to Guo; Guo boasted to the crowd: "Quan depends on my nurturing; if I show a little authority he will have no leisure but to run."
translations.idiomatic: Quan wrote from Shandong. Guo boasted to his staff: "Quan lives on my favor. Show a little authority and he will come running."

sentences.zh: ”全固留青州，國不能致。

translations.literal: " Quan remained at Qingzhou and Guo could not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan stayed in Qingzhou, and Guo could not summon him.

sentences.zh: 四月，全遣小吏致再書，國喜，曲加勞接，即日真補承信郎，冀結其心。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Quan sent a minor clerk with a second letter; Guo rejoiced, treated him with special courtesy and comfort, and that same day truly appointed him Gentleman for Fostering Trust, hoping to win his heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Quan sent a clerk with another letter. Guo was delighted, treated him with special courtesy, and that same day appointed him Gentleman for Fostering Trust, hoping to win Quan over.

sentences.zh: 小吏曰：“小吏奉書而遽得命，諸將校謂何？

translations.literal: The clerk said: "This clerk bore a letter and abruptly received an appointment—what will the generals and officers say?"
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said: "I merely delivered a letter and received an appointment at once—what will the generals say?"

sentences.zh: ”不受，歸語其徒以為笑。

translations.literal: " He would not accept it and returned to tell his followers, who took it as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and returned to tell his men, who laughed at Guo.

sentences.zh: 國見全無來朝，數致厚饋，邀全議事。

translations.literal: Guo, seeing Quan did not come to court, repeatedly sent rich gifts and invited Quan to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Quan would not come, Guo repeatedly sent rich gifts and invited him to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 會劉慶福亦使人覘國意向，國左右知之，語覘者曰：“制置無害汝等意。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Liu Qingfu also sent someone to spy on Guo's intentions; Guo's attendants learned of this and told the spy: "The commissioner means no harm to you."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingfu also sent someone to probe Guo's intentions. Guo's attendants told the spy: "The commissioner means you no harm."

sentences.zh: ”慶福以報全，全集將校曰：“我不參制閫，則曲在我。

translations.literal: " Qingfu reported this to Quan; Quan gathered his officers and said: "If I do not attend the commandery staff, the fault is mine."
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu reported this to Quan, who told his officers: "If I do not visit headquarters, the fault will be mine."

sentences.zh: 今不計生死必往見。

translations.literal: Now, regardless of life or death, I must go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: I will go regardless of the risk."

sentences.zh: ”八月，全上謁，賓讚戒全曰：“節使當庭趨，制使必免禮。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month Quan went up to pay his respects; the usher warned Quan: "The military governor should perform court advance; the commissioner is sure to waive the ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Quan went to pay his respects. The usher warned him: "Perform the court advance—the commissioner is sure to waive the ceremony."

sentences.zh: ”及庭趨，國端坐納全拜，不為止。

translations.literal: " When he performed court advance, Guo sat upright and accepted Quan's bow without stopping him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan performed the advance, but Guo sat upright and accepted his bow without waiving it.

sentences.zh: 全退，怒曰：“庭參亦常禮，全歸本朝，拜人多矣，但恨汝非文臣，本與我等。

translations.literal: Quan withdrew and angrily said: "Court audience is also an ordinary rite; Quan has returned to the dynasty and bowed to many people—only I regret that you are not a civil official; you were originally one of us."
translations.idiomatic: Quan withdrew in anger: "Court audience is ordinary courtesy. I have bowed to many since returning to the Song—only I regret you are not a military man like us."

sentences.zh: 汝向以淮西都統謁賈制帥，亦免汝拜。

translations.literal: When you once as Huaidong overall commander called on Commissioner Jia, he too waived your bow.
translations.idiomatic: When you called on Commissioner Jia as Huaidong commander, he waived your bow too.

sentences.zh: 汝有何勳業，一旦位我上，便不相假借耶？

translations.literal: What merit do you have, that overnight you sit above me and will not yield even a little?
translations.idiomatic: What merit do you have to sit above me overnight and refuse even this courtesy?

sentences.zh: 全赤心報朝廷，不反也。

translations.literal: Quan serves the court with a loyal heart and will not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: I serve the court loyally and am no rebel."

sentences.zh: ”國繼設盛會宴全，遺勞加厚，全終不樂。

translations.literal: " Guo then set a grand feast for Quan and sent ever richer gifts and comfort, yet Quan was never pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Guo then held a grand feast and sent ever richer gifts, but Quan remained displeased.

sentences.zh: 國之客章夢先主幕議，慶福謁見，夢先責客將，令隔簾貌喏，慶福不能堪。

translations.literal: Guo's guest Zhang Mengxian directed staff planning; Qingfu came to call; Mengxian rebuked the guest officer and had him perform a distant bow behind a screen; Qingfu could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's adviser Zhang Mengxian directed staff affairs. When Qingfu came to call, Mengxian had him bow from behind a screen. Qingfu was humiliated.

sentences.zh: 國以名馬十餘噭遺全，不受。

translations.literal: Guo sent more than ten famous horses as gifts to Quan; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Guo sent more than ten fine horses as gifts; Quan refused them.

sentences.zh: 國固遣，全俟其充斥階庭，伺候移時，而復卻之。

translations.literal: Guo insisted on sending them; Quan waited until they filled the steps and courtyard, watched for a long while, and then sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Guo insisted. Quan waited until the horses filled the courtyard, watched for a long while, and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 如是者半月，卒不受。

translations.literal: This went on for half a month, and in the end he never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This continued for half a month, and in the end he never accepted.

sentences.zh: 全欲往青州，懼國苛留，自計曰：“彼所爭者拜也，拜而得志，吾何愛焉！

translations.literal: Quan wished to go to Qingzhou but feared Guo would detain him harshly; he reckoned to himself: "What he contests is the bow; if bowing brings success, what do I cherish!"
translations.idiomatic: Quan wished to go to Qingzhou but feared Guo would detain him. He reckoned: "What he wants is the bow. If bowing secures my purpose, what do I lose?"

sentences.zh: ”更折節為禮。

translations.literal: He further restrained his conduct and showed courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He redoubled his deference and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 因會，席間出劄白事，國見其細故，判從之，全即席再拜謝。

translations.literal: At a meeting, during the feast he presented a memorial stating his business; Guo saw it was a trivial matter and approved it; Quan immediately bowed twice at the seat in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet, Quan submitted a memorial on a minor matter. Guo approved it, and Quan bowed twice in thanks right there at the table.

sentences.zh: 自是動息必請，得請必拜，國大喜，語家人曰：“吾折伏此虜矣。

translations.literal: From then on, every movement or rest required permission; whenever permission was granted he bowed; Guo was greatly pleased and told his family: "I have subdued this barbarian."
translations.idiomatic: From then on Quan sought permission for every move; each time it was granted, he bowed. Guo was delighted and told his household, "I have broken this fellow."

sentences.zh: ”義斌求趙邦永來山東，全為白之，國諾。

translations.literal: Yibin requested that Zhao Bangyong come to Shandong; Quan spoke on his behalf, and Guo assented.
translations.idiomatic: Yibin asked that Zhao Bangyong be sent to Shandong. Quan interceded for him, and Guo agreed.

sentences.zh: 邦永乘間告國曰：“邦永若去，制使誰與處？

translations.literal: Bangyong seized an opportunity to tell Guo: "If Bangyong goes, who will the commissioner deal with?"
translations.idiomatic: Bangyong took a moment alone with Guo and said, "If I leave, who will you have to work with?"

sentences.zh: ”國曰：“我自能兵，爾毋過慮。

translations.literal: Guo said: "I can handle military affairs myself; you need not worry excessively."
translations.idiomatic: Guo replied, "I can manage the army on my own. You worry too much."

sentences.zh: ”邦永泣而辭之。

translations.literal: Bangyong wept and took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyong wept as he bade farewell.

sentences.zh: 全遂往青州。

translations.literal: Quan then went to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then departed for Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，國集兩淮馬步軍十三萬，大閱楚城之外，以挫北人之心。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Guo assembled one hundred thirty thousand cavalry and infantry from the two Huai regions and held a grand review outside Chuzhou city to dampen the spirits of the northerners.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Guo mustered 130,000 cavalry and infantry from the two Huai circuits and held a grand military review outside Chuzhou to crush northern morale.

sentences.zh: 楊氏及軍校留者恐其圖己，內自為備。

translations.literal: Lady Yang and the officers who remained feared they were plotting against them and prepared themselves internally.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang and the officers left behind feared a plot against them and quietly made their own preparations.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年，湖州人潘甫與其從弟丙、壬起兵，密告全黨於山陽，全黨欲坐致成敗，然其謀而不助之力。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoqing, Pan Fu of Huzhou and his cousins Bing and Ren raised troops, secretly informing Quan's faction at Shanyang; Quan's faction wished to achieve success or failure without effort, but knowing of the plot, did not assist with force.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoqing, Pan Fu of Huzhou and his cousins Bing and Ren took up arms and secretly notified Quan's allies at Shanyang. The rebels hoped to reap the outcome without lifting a finger, but though they knew of the plot, they sent no help.

sentences.zh: 甫歸，陰勒部曲及聚販鹽盜至千餘，結束如北軍，率眾揚言自山陽來擁立濟王，事見《竑傳》。

translations.literal: Fu returned, secretly mustered his troops and gathered salt smugglers to more than a thousand, dressed like northern troops, and led the crowd proclaiming they had come from Shanyang to install the Prince of Ji as emperor; the affair is recorded in the biography of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fu returned home, secretly rallied his followers and salt smugglers until they numbered more than a thousand, outfitted them like Jin troops, and marched under the banner of coming from Shanyang to enthrone the Prince of Ji. The affair is treated in Hong's biography.

sentences.zh: 時全圖國之意已決，遣慶福還楚城，使為亂。

translations.literal: At this time Quan's plan against Guo was decided; he sent Qingfu back to Chuzhou to cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: By then Quan had settled on moving against Guo and sent Qingfu back to Chuzhou to stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 或教楊氏畜一妄男子，間指謂人曰：“此宗室也。

translations.literal: Some advised Lady Yang to keep a random young man and, from time to time, point and tell people: "This is an imperial clansman."
translations.idiomatic: Some counseled Lady Yang to keep a stray young man on hand and now and then point him out, saying, "This is a member of the imperial clan."

sentences.zh: ” 至語郡僚曰：“會令汝為朝士。

translations.literal: She also told the prefectural staff: "I will make you court officials."
translations.idiomatic: She also told the prefectural staff, "When the time comes, I will make you court officials."

sentences.zh: ”潛約盱眙四軍相應。

translations.literal: She secretly arranged for the four armies of Xuyi to respond in concert.
translations.idiomatic: She secretly arranged for the four Xuyi garrisons to rise in support.

sentences.zh: 忠義統領王文信有眾八百，涉徙刺揚州強勇軍。

translations.literal: Wang Wenxin, commander of the Zhongyi army, had eight hundred men and had been transferred to garrison the Qiangyong army at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenxin, commander of the Loyalty-and-Righteousness force, commanded eight hundred men and had lately been transferred to garrison Yangzhou's Strong-and-Brave Army.

sentences.zh: 國之聚兵大閱，文信在焉，慶福與謀，令歸襲揚州，別遣將劫寶應，事濟即揮眾度江。

translations.literal: When Guo assembled troops for the grand review, Wenxin was present; Qingfu plotted with him, ordering him to return and strike Yangzhou, separately dispatching generals to raid Baoying; once the affair succeeded, he was to lead the troops across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxin was present at Guo's grand review. Qingfu conspired with him to turn back and seize Yangzhou while other generals raided Baoying; once that succeeded, they would cross the Yangtze with the whole force.

sentences.zh: 盱眙四將不從，於是慶福等謀中輟，止欲快意於許國焉。

translations.literal: The four generals of Xuyi would not follow; thus Qingfu and the others' central plan stalled, and they only wanted to take satisfaction on Xu Guo.
translations.idiomatic: The four Xuyi commanders refused to cooperate, so Qingfu's wider scheme collapsed. They settled for settling scores with Xu Guo alone.

sentences.zh: 計議官苟夢玉知之，以告國，國曰：“但使反，反即殺，我豈文儒不知兵耶？

translations.literal: Planning officer Gou Mengyu learned of it and told Guo; Guo said: "Just let them rebel; when they rebel I will kill them. Do you think I am a literary scholar who does not know warfare?"
translations.idiomatic: Planning officer Gou Mengyu found out and reported it to Guo. Guo said, "Let them rebel. The moment they do, I'll kill them. Do you take me for some bookish official who knows nothing of war?"

sentences.zh: ”夢玉懼禍及己，求檄往盱眙，復告慶福曰：“制帥欲圖汝。

translations.literal: Mengyu, fearing disaster would reach him, requested an order to go to Xuyi, and again told Qingfu: "The commissioner wants to eliminate you."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be implicated, Mengyu asked for orders to go to Xuyi and then warned Qingfu, "The commissioner is plotting against you."

sentences.zh: ”兩為自結之計。

translations.literal: Each side thus made plans to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides then began scheming to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，國晨起蒞事，忽露刃充庭，客駭走，國厲聲曰：“不得無禮！
