translations.literal: On yimao day, Guo rose in the morning to attend to affairs; suddenly swords were drawn filling the courtyard; guests fled in terror; Guo shouted sternly: "Do not be rude!"
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day, Guo came out in the morning to handle business when armed men suddenly filled the courtyard. Guests fled in panic. Guo shouted, "Show some respect!"

sentences.zh: ”矢已及顙，流血蔽面，國走。

translations.literal: An arrow already reached his forehead; blood covered his face; Guo fled.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck his forehead; blood streamed down his face, and Guo ran.

sentences.zh: 亂兵悉害其家，大縱火，焚官寺，兩司積蓄盡入賊。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers all harmed his family, set fires widely, burned official temples, and all the accumulated stores of the two departments fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers slaughtered his family, set fires across the city, burned government temples, and looted everything the two bureaus had stockpiled.

sentences.zh: 親兵數十人翼國登城樓，縋城走，伏道堂中宿焉。

translations.literal: Several dozen personal guards shielded Guo as he ascended the city tower; he was lowered by rope from the wall and fled, hiding overnight at Daotang.
translations.idiomatic: A few dozen personal guards escorted Guo up the city tower. He was lowered over the wall by rope and spent the night hiding at Daotang.

sentences.zh: 時四明人姚翀通判青州，全豫令還山陽，及漣水而復止之。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Chong of Siming was assistant prefect of Qingzhou; Quan had preemptively ordered him back to Shanyang, and when he reached Lianshui had him stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong of Siming was then assistant prefect of Qingzhou. Quan had already ordered him back toward Shanyang, then halted him again when he reached Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 至是，擁翀入城，與通判宋恭喝犒南北軍，使歸營。

translations.literal: At this point they escorted Chong into the city, and with assistant prefect Song Gong called out rewards to the northern and southern armies, telling them to return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Now they ushered Chong into the city. He and Assistant Prefect Song Gong announced rewards for the northern and southern troops and sent them back to their camps.

sentences.zh: 是日，慶福首殺夢先以報貌喏之辱，戒諸軍毋害苟夢玉家，護以五十兵。

translations.literal: That day, Qingfu first killed Mengxian to avenge the insult of the distant bow, and ordered the armies not to harm Gou Mengyu's family, protecting them with fifty soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Qingfu killed Mengxian first to pay back the humiliation of the bow from behind the screen. He forbade anyone to touch Gou Mengyu's household and posted fifty men to guard them.

sentences.zh: 初，國倚揚州強勇軍統制彭興及淮西親兵將趙社、朱虎等為腹心，至是首降賊，且助為亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guo had relied on Peng Xing, commander of Yangzhou's Qiangyong army, and the Huaidong personal-troop commanders Zhao She and Zhu Hu as his inner circle; now they were the first to surrender to the rebels and even helped cause the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Guo had trusted Peng Xing, commander of Yangzhou's Strong-and-Brave Army, and his Huaidong personal commanders Zhao She and Zhu Hu above all others. Now they were the first to defect and helped carry out the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 惟丁勝、張世雄、沈興、杜靖毗、富道不屈，或與賊巷戰，興手殺賊將馬良。

translations.literal: Only Ding Sheng, Zhang Shixiong, Shen Xing, Du Jingpi, and Fu Dao refused to submit; some fought the rebels in the streets, and Xing personally killed the rebel commander Ma Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ding Sheng, Zhang Shixiong, Shen Xing, Du Jingpi, and Fu Dao held out. Some fought the rebels in the alleys, and Shen Xing personally killed the rebel officer Ma Liang.

sentences.zh: 賊黨得志，更相賀，獨張正忠歎曰：“若曹不識事體，朝廷豈置汝耶？

translations.literal: The rebel faction achieved their aim and congratulated one another; only Zhang Zhengzhong sighed and said: "You people do not understand the situation—will the court spare you?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels exulted and congratulated one another. Only Zhang Zhengzhong sighed and said, "You fools don't grasp what you've done. Do you think the court will let you live?"

sentences.zh: ”王文信復獻計慶福曰：“我偽作重傷，提本部軍歸揚州，揚守必不疑，我生縛守，以其城獻。

translations.literal: Wang Wenxin again offered a plan to Qingfu: "I will feign serious wounds, lead my unit back to Yangzhou; the Yangzhou defender will surely not suspect; I will capture the prefect alive and present the city."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenxin proposed another scheme to Qingfu: "I'll pretend to be badly wounded and march my unit back to Yangzhou. The prefect won't suspect a thing. I'll take him alive and hand over the city."

sentences.zh: ”慶福喜，夜飲而遣之。

translations.literal: Qingfu was pleased, drank through the night, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu was delighted, feasted him through the night, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，許國縊於途。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, Xu Guo hanged himself on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, Xu Guo hanged himself along the road.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，文信將至揚州，其徒有亡入城告變者。

translations.literal: On dingsi day, Wenxin was about to reach Yangzhou when some of his followers fled into the city to report the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, as Wenxin neared Yangzhou, some of his men slipped into the city and reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 時揚之兵皆在楚，知州兼提點刑獄汪統會同官議，鈐轄趙拱曰：“若不納，則文信必曰：‘我歸營，何故見拒？

translations.literal: At the time all of Yangzhou's troops were at Chuzhou; Prefect and Judicial Intendant Wang Tong gathered with fellow officials; Commandant Zhao Gong said: "If we do not admit him, Wenxin will say, 'I am returning to camp—why am I refused?'"
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou's troops were all at Chuzhou. Prefect and Judicial Intendant Wang Tong met with his staff. Commandant Zhao Gong said, "If we refuse him entry, Wenxin will claim he was only returning to camp and ask why we turned him away."

sentences.zh: ’將借是以魚肉城外之民。

translations.literal: He will use this as pretext to tyrannize the people outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He'll use that excuse to prey on the people outside the walls."

sentences.zh: 拱素善文信，請說止其兵，而以單騎入，俟入城而殺之，然後撫其兵，領往盱眙，分隸張、范戲下。

translations.literal: Gong had always been friendly with Wenxin and asked to persuade him to halt his troops, then enter alone on horseback; once inside the city, kill him, then pacify his soldiers and lead them to Xuyi to be assigned under Zhang and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, who had long been on good terms with Wenxin, volunteered to talk him into halting his men and entering the city alone. Once inside, they would kill him, calm his troops, and march them to Xuyi to be placed under Zhang and Fan.

sentences.zh: ”統喜，遣之。

translations.literal: Tong was pleased and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong agreed and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 遇文信於十里頭，置酒相勞苦，文信偽為裹創狀。

translations.literal: He met Wenxin at Shilitou, set out wine to comfort him, and Wenxin faked being bandaged for wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He met Wenxin at Shilitou, set out wine, and Wenxin played the part of a man wrapped in bandages.

sentences.zh: 拱曰：“忠義反楚州，揚州人見忠義暮歸，豈不相疑？

translations.literal: Gong said: "Zhongyi rebelled at Chuzhou; Yangzhou people see Zhongyi returning at dusk—will they not be suspicious?"
translations.idiomatic: Gong said, "The Loyalty-and-Righteousness force rebelled at Chuzhou. When Yangzhou folk see them riding in at dusk, won't they panic?"

sentences.zh: 不若暫駐兵城外，然後同見提刑，提刑急欲知楚州事也。

translations.literal: Better to temporarily station troops outside the city, then together see the judicial intendant; the judicial intendant urgently wants to know about Chuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave your men outside for now and come in with me to see the judicial intendant. He is desperate for news from Chuzhou."

sentences.zh: ”文信不疑，聯騎入城，坐客次。

translations.literal: Wenxin did not suspect; they entered the city riding together and sat in the guest hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxin saw no trap. The two rode in together and waited in the reception hall.

sentences.zh: 拱先入，勸統收戮之，統躊躇不敢發。

translations.literal: Gong entered first and urged Tong to arrest and execute him; Tong hesitated and dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: Gong went in first and pressed Tong to seize and kill Wenxin, but Tong wavered and could not bring himself to act.

sentences.zh: 劉全知其謀，帥甲士突入郡堂，厲聲曰：“王統領好人，提刑不必疑，請出受參。

translations.literal: Liu Quan knew the plot, led armored soldiers into the prefectural hall, and shouted sternly: "Commander Wang is a good man; Judicial Intendant, you need not suspect—please come out to receive salute."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan, who knew the plan, burst into the prefectural hall at the head of armored men and shouted, "Commander Wang means well! Prefect, there is nothing to fear—please come out and receive our salute."

sentences.zh: ”統不得已，出而犒之。

translations.literal: Tong had no choice but to come out and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had no choice but to come out and treat them to refreshments.

sentences.zh: 劉全以兵翼之出，館其家。

translations.literal: Liu Quan escorted him out with troops and housed him at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan surrounded him with soldiers, escorted him out, and kept him at his own house.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，統未有處。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, Tong had not yet decided what to do.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the next day, Tong still had not settled on a course of action.

sentences.zh: 拱又請引文信出城，與議回屯楚州。

translations.literal: Gong again asked to lead Wenxin out of the city to discuss returning to garrison Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong again asked to take Wenxin outside the walls to discuss sending the troops back to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文信知事泄，拱就出，劉全亦請從。

translations.literal: Wenxin knew the affair was leaked; Gong then went out, and Liu Quan also asked to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxin realized the plot had leaked. Gong went out, and Liu Quan asked to go along.

sentences.zh: 至平山堂，文信責拱賣己，欲殺之，拱曰：“爾謀如此，三城人命何辜！

translations.literal: At Pingshan Hall, Wenxin rebuked Gong for betraying him and wanted to kill him; Gong said: "With your plan like this, what crime do the people of the three cities have!"
translations.idiomatic: At Pingshan Hall, Wenxin accused Gong of selling him out and tried to kill him. Gong cried, "With a scheme like yours, what did the people of three cities do to deserve this?"

sentences.zh: 我已存三城人，身死無憾。

translations.literal: I have already saved the people of the three cities; if I die I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: I have already saved the people of three cities. If I die for it, I have no regrets."

sentences.zh: 然我死，汝八百家老幼在城，豈得生耶？

translations.literal: Yet if I die, your eight hundred households of old and young in the city—can they live?"
translations.idiomatic: But if you kill me, what becomes of the eight hundred families—young and old—still inside the city?"

sentences.zh: ”文信及其眾動色，文信、劉全遂還楚州。

translations.literal: Wenxin and his followers changed color; Wenxin and Liu Quan then returned to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxin and his men fell silent. Wenxin and Liu Quan then withdrew to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時盱眙總管夏全聞山陽得志，亦懷異圖，劉卓厚賂之，乃止。

translations.literal: At the time Xuyi commander Xia Quan heard Shanyang had succeeded and also harbored rebellious intent; Liu Zhuo heavily bribed him, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuyi commander Xia Quan heard that the rebels had succeeded at Shanyang, he too began nursing rebellious designs. Liu Zhuo bribed him heavily, and he held back.

sentences.zh: 及文信亂，卓懼夏全復動，乃使卞整將兵三千視之，使不敢動。

translations.literal: When Wenxin rebelled, Zhuo feared Xia Quan would stir again, so he sent Bian Zheng with three thousand troops to watch him and keep him from moving.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxin's revolt, Zhuo feared Xia Quan might move again and sent Bian Zheng with three thousand men to keep an eye on him and prevent any action.

sentences.zh: 整以邀文信為辭，引兵還揚州，因偽言盱眙失守，卞整為亂，於是揚州復震，城門晝閉。

translations.literal: Zheng used inviting Wenxin as pretext, led troops back to Yangzhou, and falsely reported that Xuyi had fallen and Bian Zheng had rebelled; Yangzhou was shaken again, and the city gates were closed by day.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Zheng used the excuse of meeting Wenxin to march back to Yangzhou and spread the false report that Xuyi had fallen and that he himself had rebelled. Yangzhou was thrown into panic again, and the gates were shut even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 彌遠懼激他變，欲姑事涵忍而後圖之。

translations.literal: Miyuan feared provoking other changes and wished to temporarily tolerate and bear with it, then deal with it later.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan feared setting off further upheaval and decided to swallow the insult for the moment and plan his response later.

sentences.zh: 謀帥莫可，以徐晞稷嘗倅楚州、守海州，得全歡心，晞稷亦勇往，乃授淮東制置使，令出屈撫全。

translations.literal: No suitable commander could be found; because Xu Xiji had once served as vice prefect at Chuzhou and prefect at Haizhou, winning Quan's favor, and Xiji was also bold in going forward, he was appointed Huaidong commissioner and ordered to go out and humbly soothe Quan.
translations.idiomatic: No obvious choice emerged for overall command. Xu Xiji had once served as vice prefect at Chuzhou and prefect at Haizhou, had won Quan's goodwill, and was bold enough to take the post. He was therefore made Huaidong commissioner and sent out to placate Quan.

sentences.zh: 時慶福以事濟報全，全又牒義斌等曰：“許國謀反，已伏誅矣，爾軍並聽我節制。

translations.literal: At the time Qingfu reported success to Quan; Quan also sent a dispatch to Yibin and others saying: "Xu Guo plotted rebellion and has already been executed; your armies shall all obey my command."
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu reported their success to Quan, who then issued a dispatch to Yibin and the others: "Xu Guo plotted rebellion and has been put to death. All your forces are now under my command."

sentences.zh: ”義斌得牒大罵曰：“逆賊背國厚恩，擅殺制使。

translations.literal: Yibin received the dispatch and cursed loudly: "The traitor rebel has betrayed the state's great favor and murdered the commissioner on his own authority."
translations.idiomatic: When Yibin received the dispatch he raged, "That traitor has thrown away the state's great kindness and murdered the commissioner on his own authority."

sentences.zh: 此事皆因我起，我必報此仇。

translations.literal: This affair all began because of me; I will surely avenge this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: This whole disaster started because of me. I will have my revenge."

sentences.zh: ”呼趙邦永曰：“趙二，汝南人，正須爾明此事。

translations.literal: He called Zhao Bangyong: "Zhao the Second, you southerner—you precisely need to clarify this affair."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zhao Bangyong: "Zhao the Second—you're a man of the south. You're the one who must make this plain to the world."

sentences.zh: ”乃斬齎牒人，南向告天誓眾，見者憤激。

translations.literal: He then beheaded the dispatch bearer, faced south to inform Heaven, and swore before the assembly; those who saw it were stirred to fury.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the messenger who had brought the dispatch, turned south toward Heaven, and swore an oath before the troops. All who witnessed it burned with outrage.

sentences.zh: 全自青州至楚城，佯責慶福不能彈壓，致忠義之哄，斬數人，請待罪，朝廷未之詰。

translations.literal: Quan came from Qingzhou to Chuzhou, feigned to blame Qingfu for failing to suppress and causing Zhongyi's uproar, executed several men, and requested punishment; the court did not investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan returned from Qingzhou to Chuzhou, pretended to rebuke Qingfu for failing to keep order and letting the Loyalty-and-Righteousness force run riot, executed several men, and asked to be punished. The court did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 趙範時知揚州兼提點刑獄，得制置印於潰卒中，以授晞稷。

translations.literal: Zhao Fan was then prefect and judicial intendant of Yangzhou; he recovered the commissioner's seal from scattered soldiers and gave it to Xiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan was then prefect and judicial intendant of Yangzhou. He recovered the commissioner's seal from fleeing soldiers and handed it to Xiji.

sentences.zh: 全遣騎逆晞稷。

translations.literal: Quan sent riders to welcome Xiji.
translations.idiomatic: Quan sent horsemen out to welcome Xiji.

sentences.zh: 己卯，晞稷入楚城。

translations.literal: On jimao day, Xiji entered Chuzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day, Xiji entered Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉全躍馬登郡廳，晞稷迎之，全及門下馬，拜庭下，晞稷降等止之，賊眾乃悅。

translations.literal: Liu Quan leaped on his horse and ascended the prefectural hall; Xiji welcomed him; Quan dismounted at the gate and bowed in the courtyard; Xiji descended rank to stop him, and the rebel masses were then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan galloped up to the prefectural hall, where Xiji received him. Quan dismounted at the gate and bowed in the courtyard. Xiji stepped down to raise him up, and the rebel troops were satisfied.

sentences.zh: 四月，潘壬變姓名至楚州，將度淮而北，小校明亮獲之，械送行在伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Pan Ren changed his name and came to Chuzhou, intending to cross the Huai north; Junior Officer Ming Liang captured him, fettered him, and sent him to the capital, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Pan Ren assumed a false name and reached Chuzhou, planning to cross the Huai northward. Junior Officer Ming Liang seized him, put him in chains, and sent him to the capital for execution.

sentences.zh: 甲午，時青使人偽為金兵，道邳州，出漣水，奪全田租而伏騎八百。

translations.literal: On jiawu day, Shi Qing sent men disguised as Jin troops, passed through Pizhou, exited at Lianshui, seized Quan's land rent, and lay in ambush with eight hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day, Shi Qing sent men disguised as Jin soldiers through Pizhou and out at Lianshui, where they seized Quan's collected land rents and hid eight hundred cavalry in ambush.

sentences.zh: 翼旦，全引二百騎度淮與鬥。

translations.literal: The next morning, Quan led two hundred cavalry to cross the Huai and fight.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Quan crossed the Huai with two hundred horsemen to give battle.

sentences.zh: 伏發，全敗，圍之，慶福以兵往拔全出。

translations.literal: The ambush struck; Quan was defeated and surrounded; Qingfu led troops to rescue Quan.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang; Quan was beaten and surrounded until Qingfu marched out and fought his way in to pull him free.

sentences.zh: 全與慶福俱重傷，歸楚州。

translations.literal: Quan and Qingfu were both seriously wounded and returned to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Qingfu were both badly wounded and limped back to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁勝、張世雄欲乘全敗舉兵追北軍，晞稷止之。

translations.literal: Ding Sheng and Zhang Shixiong wished to take advantage of Quan's defeat to raise troops and pursue the northern army; Xiji stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Sheng and Zhang Shixiong wanted to exploit Quan's defeat, raise troops, and chase the northern force. Xiji forbade it.

sentences.zh: 全後知其謀，對晞稷詰之，二人不為屈。

translations.literal: Quan later learned of their plot and questioned Xiji about it; the two would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Quan later learned of the plan and confronted Xiji about it. Ding and Zhang refused to back down.

sentences.zh: 然懼禍及己，晞稷乃潛授世雄雄勝軍統制，教使逃而陽索之。

translations.literal: Yet fearing disaster for himself, Xiji secretly appointed Shixiong commander of the Xiongsheng army, instructing him to flee while publicly searching for him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisals, Xiji secretly made Shixiong commander of the Xiongsheng Army, told him to flee, and then pretended to hunt for him.

sentences.zh: 北軍追世雄，世雄且戰且走，得達揚州。

translations.literal: The northern army pursued Shixiong; Shixiong fought while retreating and reached Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops pursued Shixiong, but he fought a fighting retreat all the way to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晞稷初至楚，緩急相濟，如囚趙社，逐朱虎，賊尚知畏。

translations.literal: When Xiji first arrived at Chuzhou, in emergencies they helped each other—such as imprisoning Zhao She and expelling Zhu Hu—and the rebels still knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiji first reached Chuzhou, he and Quan still cooperated in a pinch—imprisoning Zhao She, driving out Zhu Hu—and the rebels still showed some fear.

sentences.zh: 屢令全還戰馬、軍器於制司，全唯唯。

translations.literal: He repeatedly ordered Quan to return war horses and weapons to the commissionerate; Quan agreed verbally.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly demanded that Quan return war horses and arms to the commissionerate. Quan murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 退招姚翀及將校飲，酒酣，全曰：“ 制司追我戰馬、軍器，若何？

translations.literal: Afterwards he invited Yao Chong and the officers to drink; when drunk, Quan said: "The commissionerate demands my war horses and weapons back—what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: Later he invited Yao Chong and his officers to drink. When the wine was deep, Quan asked, "The commissionerate wants my horses and weapons back. What do we do?"

sentences.zh: ”忽有將校曰：“當時忠義隻百十人，其他軍皆南軍乘勢將帶，若潰將何以還？

translations.literal: Suddenly an officer said: "At the time Zhongyi had only a hundred-odd men; all the other troops were southern-army officers who seized the opportunity to become commanders—if we disperse, how can the generals return?"
translations.idiomatic: One officer blurted out, "The Loyalty-and-Righteousness force was only a hundred-odd men. Every other unit was a southern officer who grabbed a command when the moment came. If we break up now, how do the generals go home?"

sentences.zh: ”一人曰：“制司必欲追之，不若有官者棄官，無官者歸山東為百姓。

translations.literal: One man said: "If the commissionerate must recover them, better that those with offices resign, and those without return to Shandong as commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "If the commissionerate insists on taking them back, let men with rank resign and the rest go home to Shandong as farmers."

sentences.zh: ”一人抵掌憤然，使全反，全陽罵之。

translations.literal: One man clapped his hands indignantly, urging Quan to rebel; Quan feigned to curse him.
translations.idiomatic: A third man slapped his knee in fury and urged Quan to rebel. Quan pretended to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 翀以告晞稷。

translations.literal: Chong reported this to Xiji.
translations.idiomatic: Chong reported the conversation to Xiji.

sentences.zh: 翼日，全見晞稷求納官，晞稷撫之而去。

translations.literal: The next day, Quan saw Xiji seeking to surrender his office; Xiji comforted him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Quan visited Xiji and offered to resign his commission. Xiji soothed him and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 自是不復誰何，其後至以“恩府”稱全、“恩堂”稱楊氏，而手足倒置矣。

translations.literal: From then on no one held him accountable; afterwards they even called Quan "Benefactor Mansion" and Lady Yang "Benefactor Hall," and roles were completely inverted.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one dared hold Quan to account. Before long they were calling him "Benefactor's Mansion" and Lady Yang "Benefactor's Hall"—superior and subordinate turned upside down.

sentences.zh: 軍器庫止餘槍幹數千，全復取去。

translations.literal: The arsenal had only a few thousand spear shafts left; Quan took them again.
translations.idiomatic: The arms depot held only a few thousand spear shafts; Quan took those too.

sentences.zh: 全欲戰艦，晞稷使擇二艘。

translations.literal: Quan wanted warships; Xiji had him choose two.
translations.idiomatic: Quan asked for warships, and Xiji let him pick two.

sentences.zh: 全移出淮河，使軍習之。

translations.literal: Quan moved them out onto the Huai River and had the army drill with them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had them moved onto the Huai and put his men through drills on the water.

sentences.zh: 初，楚城之將亂也，有吏竊許國書篋二以獻慶福，皆機事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chuzhou city was about to rebel, an official stole two of Xu Guo's document cases and presented them to Qingfu; they all concerned secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Chuzhou mutiny, a clerk stole two of Xu Guo's document cases and handed them to Qingfu. They were full of confidential business.

sentences.zh: 慶福賞盜篋者五百千，未之閱。

translations.literal: Qingfu rewarded the case thief five hundred strings of cash without having read them.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu gave the thief five hundred strings of cash and never opened the cases.

sentences.zh: 全始發緘，使家僮讀之，有廟堂遺國書令圖全者，全大怒；

translations.literal: Quan only then broke the seals, had a household servant read them, and found a letter from the court to Guo ordering a plot against Quan; Quan was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Quan break the seals and have a household servant read them aloud. One letter from court to Guo ordered a plot against Quan. Quan flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 又有苟夢玉書，即以慶福謀告國者，全始惡夢玉反覆。

translations.literal: There was also Gou Mengyu's letter revealing that Qingfu's plot had been reported to Guo; Quan then came to hate Mengyu's double-dealing.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a letter from Gou Mengyu showing he had warned Guo about Qingfu's conspiracy. Quan now despised Mengyu as a double-dealer.

sentences.zh: 夢玉知之，時已被堂召，亟辭全如京。

translations.literal: Mengyu learned of this; he had already been summoned by the court and urgently took leave of Quan for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengyu learned of this, he had already received a summons to court and hurried to take his leave of Quan for the capital.

sentences.zh: 己卯，全饋餞夢玉如平時，潛殪諸十里之郊，復出榜捕害夢玉者。

translations.literal: On jimao day, Quan sent farewell gifts as usual, secretly murdered him in the suburbs ten li out, then posted a proclamation seeking the killer of Mengyu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day, Quan saw him off with gifts as if nothing were amiss, then had him killed in secret ten li outside the city and posted a reward for whoever had murdered Mengyu.

sentences.zh: 全往青州。

translations.literal: Quan went to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan departed for Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月丁卯，全取東平，不克。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the fifth month, Quan attacked Dongping but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day of the fifth month, Quan attacked Dongping but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，劉全以券易制司錢，不如欲，復謀亂，楊氏出二千緡解之，乃止。

translations.literal: On wuyin day, Liu Quan used vouchers to exchange for commissionerate money; not getting what he wanted, he again plotted rebellion; Lady Yang put up two thousand strings to settle it, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day, Liu Quan tried to cash vouchers at the commissionerate for more than he was owed. When he was refused, he plotted rebellion again. Lady Yang paid out two thousand strings to smooth things over, and the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 全引兵攻恩州。

translations.literal: Quan led troops to attack Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan led troops to attack Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 明日，義斌出兵與全鬥，全敗。

translations.literal: The next day Yibin led his army out to fight Quan, and Quan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yibin marched out to fight Quan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 義斌以千五百騎追之，獲馬二千匹，皆揚州強勇軍馬也。

translations.literal: Yibin pursued with one thousand five hundred horsemen and captured two thousand horses, all mounts of Yangzhou's Qiangyong army.
translations.idiomatic: Yibin pursued with fifteen hundred horsemen and seized two thousand horses—all from Yangzhou's Strong-and-Brave Army.

sentences.zh: 慶福往救，又敗。

translations.literal: Qingfu went to rescue him and was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu went to relieve him and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 全退保山崮，抽山陽忠義以北。

translations.literal: Quan withdrew to hold the mountain fastness and drew the Shanyang loyalists northward.
translations.idiomatic: Quan withdrew to a mountain stronghold and pulled the Shanyang loyalists north.

sentences.zh: 楊氏及劉全皆欲親赴之，會全遣人求晞稷書與義斌連和，乃止。

translations.literal: Lady Yang and Liu Quan both wished to go in person; but as Quan sent someone to ask Xiji for a letter to make peace with Yibin, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang and Liu Quan both wanted to go in person, but Quan sent for a letter from Xiji to reconcile with Yibin, and they held back.

sentences.zh: 義斌納全降兵，兵勢大振，進攻真定，降金將武仙，眾至數十萬，致書沿江制置使趙善湘曰：“不誅逆全，恢復不成。

translations.literal: Yibin accepted Quan's surrendered troops; his military power greatly revived; he advanced to attack Zhending, induced the Jin general Wu Xian to submit, and his force reached several hundred thousand; he sent a letter to the riverine commissioner Zhao Shanxiang saying: "Unless the traitor Quan is executed, recovery cannot be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Yibin took in Quan's surrendered troops, and his army swelled to hundreds of thousands. He advanced on Zhending, won over the Jin general Wu Xian, and wrote to riverine commissioner Zhao Shanxiang: "Unless the traitor Quan is put to death, the Central Plains cannot be recovered."

sentences.zh: 但能遣兵扼淮，進據漣、海以蹙之，斷其南路，如此賊者，或生禽，或斬首，惟朝廷所命。

translations.literal: If troops can be sent to hold the Huai, advance to occupy Lian and Hai to press him, and cut his southern route, then for such a bandit, whether taken alive or beheaded, it is for the court to command.
translations.idiomatic: Send troops to hold the Huai, seize Lian and Hai to squeeze him, and cut his southern line of retreat. Then this bandit may be taken alive or beheaded—as the court commands."

sentences.zh: 賊平之後，收復一京三府，然後義斌戰河北，盱眙諸將、襄陽騎士戰河南，神州可復也。

translations.literal: After the bandits are pacified and one capital and three prefectures are recovered, then Yibin can fight in Hebei, the generals of Xuyi and the horsemen of Xiangyang can fight in Henan, and the divine land can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels are crushed and the capital and three prefectures retaken, Yibin can fight in Hebei, the Xuyi generals and Xiangyang cavalry can fight in Henan, and the empire can be restored."

sentences.zh: ”時四總管亦各遣計議官致書，乞助討賊，範亦以為言，不報。

translations.literal: At the time the four overall commanders also each sent planning officers with letters asking help to suppress the bandits; Fan also spoke to this effect; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The four overall commanders also sent planning officers begging help against the rebels. Fan made the same plea. The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 全貽書制置司，誣義斌叛，晞稷繳達之。

translations.literal: Quan sent a letter to the commissionerate slandering Yibin as a rebel; Xiji forwarded it to court.
translations.idiomatic: Quan wrote the commissionerate claiming Yibin had rebelled, and Xiji forwarded the letter to court.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷知義斌之功，憚全，未欲行賞。

translations.literal: At the time the court knew Yibin's merit but feared Quan and did not yet wish to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Yibin's merit but feared Quan and held back his rewards.

sentences.zh: 未幾，義斌俟命不至，拓地而北，與大元兵戰於內黃之五馬山。

translations.literal: Before long, as orders did not arrive, Yibin extended his territory northward and fought the Great Yuan army at Wuma Mountain in Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: When orders still did not come, Yibin pushed north and fought the Mongols at Wuma Mountain in Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 大元兵說之降，義斌厲聲曰：“我大宋臣，且河北、山東皆宋民，義豈為他臣屬耶！

translations.literal: The Great Yuan army urged him to submit; Yibin said sternly: "I am a minister of Great Song, and moreover Hebei and Shandong are all Song people—how could righteousness make me subject to another!"
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols urged him to submit. Yibin declared sternly: "I am a Song subject, and Hebei and Shandong are Song lands—how could I serve another master!"

sentences.zh: ”遂死之。

translations.literal: He then died there.
translations.idiomatic: He died fighting.

sentences.zh: 戲下王義深等復歸全。

translations.literal: Wang Yishen and others among his followers returned to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yishen and others among his followers returned to Quan.

sentences.zh: 全使人說時青附己，饋金五百兩。

translations.literal: Quan sent someone to persuade Shi Qing to attach to him and gave five hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Quan sent envoys to win Shi Qing over with five hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 青見義斌死，乃附全，自移屯淮陰。

translations.literal: When Qing saw Yibin had died, he then attached to Quan and moved his camp on his own to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: After Yibin's death, Qing submitted to Quan and shifted his camp to Huaiyin on his own.

sentences.zh: 全招青入城飲，折俎銅券二千，他饋稱是，恩遍麾下，人人喜悅。

translations.literal: Quan invited Qing into the city to drink, gave two thousand copper vouchers on the folding table, and other gifts in proportion; favor spread through all his officers, and every man rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Quan feasted Qing in the city, gave him two thousand copper vouchers at table and comparable gifts besides, and spread favors through the ranks until every man was pleased.

sentences.zh: 晞稷宴青，全饋折俎如前。

translations.literal: Xiji feasted Qing, and Quan gave folding-table gifts as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji also feasted Qing, and Quan again gave gifts at table as before.

sentences.zh: 全將往山東，以南軍九百從，官犒鐵錢券人五千，全犒銅錢三倍，許攜南貨免稅。

translations.literal: Quan was about to go to Shandong with nine hundred southern troops following; the government rewarded iron-cash vouchers at five thousand per man; Quan rewarded copper cash at triple that, and permitted them to carry southern goods tax-free.
translations.idiomatic: Quan prepared to go to Shandong with nine hundred southern troops. The government paid five thousand iron-cash vouchers per man; Quan paid triple that in copper cash and let them carry southern goods tax-free.

sentences.zh: 於是請行者不已，得千人以俱，晞稷又以千八百人繼之。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who asked to go did not cease, and he obtained a thousand men to accompany him; Xiji then sent another eighteen hundred men after them.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteers kept coming until he had a thousand men to take along, and Xiji sent another eighteen hundred after them.

sentences.zh: 二年春，趙範奉祠，林珙知揚州、權提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Zhao Fan received temple stipend; Lin Qi became prefect of Yangzhou and acting judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Zhao Fan retired on temple stipend; Lin Qi became prefect of Yangzhou and acting judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 全北剽山東，南假宋以疑大元，且仰食。

translations.literal: Quan raided Shandong in the north, borrowed Song in the south to confuse the Great Yuan, and moreover lived on their provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Quan raided Shandong in the north, used the Song in the south to keep the Mongols guessing, and lived off Song provisions.

sentences.zh: 會金與大元爭大名，全得往來經理。

translations.literal: As Jin and the Great Yuan contended for Daming, Quan was able to come and go managing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin and the Mongols fought over Daming, Quan slipped back and forth managing his affairs.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰朔，大元兵攻青州，全大小百戰，終不利，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, day bingchen, the Great Yuan army attacked Qingzhou; Quan fought great and small battles numbering a hundred, was ultimately unfavorable, and shut the gates to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, the first of the third month, the Mongols attacked Qingzhou. Quan fought a hundred engagements, lost ground, and shut himself inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 大元築長圍，夜布狗砦，糧援路絕。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan built a long encirclement, laid out dog-palisades by night, and grain-supply routes were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols built a long encirclement, ringed the city with chevaux-de-frise at night, and cut off all supply routes.

sentences.zh: 全遣小校周興祖縋城，雜樵采者走楚州發援兵，終不能支。

translations.literal: Quan sent the junior officer Zhou Xingzu down the wall by rope, mixed with woodcutters to run to Chuzhou to raise relief troops, but in the end could not hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Quan sent Junior Officer Zhou Xingzu over the wall on a rope, mingling with woodcutters to reach Chuzhou for relief, but the city could not be held.

sentences.zh: 全與福謀，福曰：“二人俱死無益也，汝身係南北輕重，我當死守孤城，汝間道南歸，提兵赴援，可尋生路。

translations.literal: Quan consulted with Fu; Fu said: "For both of us to die is of no benefit; your person bears the weight of north and south; I shall die defending this lone city; you take a secret route south, bring troops to relieve us, and may find a way to live."
translations.idiomatic: Quan consulted Fu, who said: "If we both die, it helps nothing. You matter to north and south alike. I'll die holding this city. You slip south by a hidden route, raise relief, and may yet survive."

sentences.zh: ” 全曰：“數十萬敵，未易支也。

translations.literal: Quan said: "Several hundred thousand enemies are not easy to withstand."
translations.idiomatic: Quan replied, "We cannot hold against hundreds of thousands of enemies."

sentences.zh: 全朝出則城夕陷，不如兄歸。

translations.literal: If Quan leaves in the morning the city falls by evening; better that elder brother return.
translations.idiomatic: If I leave in the morning, the city falls by evening. Better you go back, brother."

sentences.zh: ”於是全止而福行。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quan stayed and Fu went.
translations.idiomatic: Quan stayed; Fu went.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初以力未能討，故用晞稷調護，及傳全被圍，稍欲圖賊。

translations.literal: At first the court, because its strength could not yet suppress him, therefore used Xiji to mediate and protect; when word spread that Quan was besieged, they slightly wished to plot against the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court, unable yet to crush him, had used Xiji to manage affairs. When word came that Quan was besieged, they began to plan against the rebel.

sentences.zh: 晞稷畏懦，幸全未歸以苟歲月。

translations.literal: Xiji was timid and cowardly, fortunate that Quan had not returned so as to scrape by month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji was timid and cowardly, relieved that Quan had not returned so he could scrape by month by month.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方謀易帥，劉卓久在盱眙，雅意建閫；

translations.literal: The court was planning to replace the commander; Liu Zhuo had long been at Xuyi and inwardly wished to establish a command post;
translations.idiomatic: The court planned to replace the commander. Liu Zhuo had long served at Xuyi and coveted a command of his own;

sentences.zh: 又見賊勢稍孤，意功名可立，使鎮江副都統彭忄乇延譽京師，自謂：“素撫鎮江，三萬人足用，且得四總管歡心，討賊有餘力。

translations.literal: he also saw the bandit force somewhat isolated and thought merit and fame could be established; he had the Zhenjiang deputy commander Peng Zhen praise him at the capital, saying himself: "I have long pacified Zhenjiang; thirty thousand men are enough, and moreover I can win the goodwill of the four overall commanders; suppressing bandits there is surplus strength."
translations.idiomatic: seeing the rebels somewhat isolated, he thought glory was within reach. He had Zhenjiang deputy commander Peng Zhen praise him at court, claiming: "I have long governed Zhenjiang; thirty thousand men are enough, the four overall commanders will follow me, and I have force to spare against the rebels."

sentences.zh: ”朝廷信之，忄乇亦垂涎代卓，從臾尤力。

translations.literal: The court believed him; Zhen also coveted replacing Zhuo and urged it with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed him. Peng Zhen also coveted Zhuo's post and pressed the case hard.

sentences.zh: 九月，以卓知楚州兼淮東制置使，

translations.literal: In the ninth month Zhuo was made prefect of Chuzhou and concurrently Huaidong pacification commissioner,
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhuo was made prefect of Chuzhou and Huaidong pacification commissioner,

sentences.zh: 忄乇代知盱眙，晞稷不知也。

translations.literal: and Zhen replaced him as prefect of Xuyi; Xiji did not know this.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhen replaced him at Xuyi—without Xiji's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 己亥，晞稷以戶部侍郎召，未幾，出知袁州。

translations.literal: On day jihai Xiji was summoned as vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue; before long he was sent out as prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day Xiji was recalled as vice minister of Revenue; soon after he was sent out as prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬子朔，卓至楚州，心知不能制馭四總管，惟以鎮江兵自隨。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, day renzi, Zhuo reached Chuzhou, knowing in his heart he could not control the four overall commanders and taking only Zhenjiang troops with him.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day, the first of the eleventh month, Zhuo reached Chuzhou. He knew he could not control the four overall commanders and brought only his Zhenjiang troops.

sentences.zh: 時青在淮陰，卓怨其移屯叛己，不召也。

translations.literal: Shi Qing was at Huaiyin; Zhuo resented that he had moved his camp in defiance and did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qing was at Huaiyin. Zhuo resented his unsanctioned move and did not summon him.

sentences.zh: 夏全請從，卓素畏全狡，亦俾留盱眙。

translations.literal: Xia Quan asked to accompany him; Zhuo had long feared Quan's craftiness and also had him remain at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Quan asked to accompany him, but Zhuo, who had long feared Xia's cunning, kept him at Xuyi as well.

sentences.zh: 忄乇自揣資望視卓更淺，曰：“卓之止夏全，是欲遺患盱眙也。

translations.literal: Zhen reckoned his standing was even shallower than Zhuo's and said: "Zhuo's keeping Xia Quan is meant to leave trouble at Xuyi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen judged his own standing even lower than Zhuo's and said, "Zhuo is leaving Xia Quan at Xuyi to plant trouble there."

sentences.zh: 卓猶憚夏全，我何能用？

translations.literal: Zhuo still fears Xia Quan—how can I be used?"
translations.idiomatic: If Zhuo still fears Xia Quan, how can I be of use?"

sentences.zh: ”乃激夏全曰：“楚城賊黨不滿三千，健將又在山東，劉制使圖之，收功在旦夕。

translations.literal: He then incited Xia Quan: "The bandits in Chuzhou are fewer than three thousand; their fierce generals are still in Shandong; Commissioner Liu is plotting against them; success is within days."
translations.idiomatic: He goaded Xia Quan: "The rebels in Chuzhou number fewer than three thousand, their best generals are in Shandong, and Commissioner Liu is closing in. Victory is only days away."

sentences.zh: 太尉曷不往赴事會，何端坐為？

translations.literal: Why does the Grand Marshal not go to seize the moment—why sit idle?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal, why not seize the moment instead of sitting idle?"

sentences.zh: ”夏全欣然領兵徑入楚城，青亦自淮陰復移屯城內。

translations.literal: Xia Quan gladly led his troops straight into Chuzhou city; Qing also moved his camp back inside the city from Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Quan gladly marched straight into Chuzhou, and Qing shifted back into the city from Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 卓且駭且恐，勢不容卻，復就二人謀焉。

translations.literal: Zhuo was both alarmed and afraid; the situation did not permit retreat, and he again consulted the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was alarmed and afraid, unable to turn them back, and consulted the two men again.

sentences.zh: 時傳全已死，福欲分兵赴援，兵少，卒不往。

translations.literal: At the time it was reported Quan had died; Fu wished to divide troops to go to his relief, but the force was small and in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors said Quan was dead. Fu wanted to send a relief detachment, but his force was too small and he never went.

sentences.zh: 甲子，卓令夏全盛陳兵楚城，賊黨震恐，楊氏遣人賂夏全求緩師，乃

translations.literal: On day jiazi Zhuo ordered Xia Quan to array his troops in full strength at Chuzhou; the rebel faction was shaken with fear; Lady Yang sent someone to bribe Xia Quan to ask for a slower advance, and then
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day Zhuo had Xia Quan parade his full strength before Chuzhou. The rebels were terrified. Lady Yang sent bribes asking Xia Quan to ease the pressure, and then
